title: Dictionaries Without Ontologies: What a Sparse Autoencoder Latent Is Evidence For, Why Decodability, Use and Reproducibility Do Not Add Up to Canonicity, and the Identifiability Premise No Real-Model Result Has Checked
abstract: Life of Research (c) 2026 Pranay Mahendrakar. Licensed under CC BY 4.0. Sparse autoencoders are now the default instrument for decomposing language model activations, and their latents are routinely reported as the model's features: units the network itself uses, which a wide enough dictionary has pulled out of superposition. This paper asks what a latent is evidence for. It separates four claims that the word "feature" runs together - that a property is linearly readable at an activation site, that the model's downstream computation depends on a direction, that the same unit recurs across training choices, and that the recurring unit is canonical, meaning unique, complete and atomic - and reads the published record against each. The record supports the first broadly, though the natural-language label attached to a latent is a weaker link than the latent itself; it supports the second unevenly, with causal roles that differ between SAE families trained on the same model; it supports the third at the grain of subspaces more readily than at the grain of individual latents; and it supports the fourth on no real language model. The reason is structural. Classical results make sparse dictionaries unique only when the data are generated by a sparse linear code meeting stated conditions; that premise has been tested only piecemeal, concept by concept, and the comparisons with a ground truth for the full dictionary that could reach canonicity have been run only on toy, synthetic, formal-language and board-game models; natural-language models have only task-specific, approximate ground truths. A short rotation argument shows how a multi-dimensional feature would produce the pattern of seed-dependent latents inside reproducible subspaces that has been reported. The paper ends with a use-indexed licensing procedure and five studies that would settle the open part. Throughout, it works from published measurements, each credited to the source that reported it.

title: A Pathological Image-Based Pathomics Signature Combined with Clinicopathological Features for Predicting Lymph Node Metastasis in Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma: A Development and External Validation Study
abstract: Background: Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) accounts for over 80% of esophageal cancer cases globally. Lymph node status is the strongest determinant of survival after resection, yet occult disease is found in about 17% of patients classified as node-negative. We developed a postoperative model estimating the probability of lymph node metastasis (LNM) from the resection specimen, combining nuclear features with clinicopathological variables. Methods: Of 477 consecutive ESCC patients undergoing radical esophagectomy without neoadjuvant therapy, 416 were analyzed (LNM 217, 52.2%). Nuclear features were extracted from H&E whole-slide images (20×) by QuPath optical-density detection; LASSO logistic regression selected 17. A nomogram combining the pathomics score with age, sex, tumor location, pT category and grade was validated by 10-fold cross-validation (out-of-fold, OOF) and applied without refitting to 101 patients from another institution. Results: OOF AUC was 0.821 (95% CI 0.779–0.858) for the combined model, versus 0.791 (clinical) and 0.762 (pathomics alone). The pathomics score remained an independent predictor (adjusted OR 2.47, 95% CI 1.80–3.39; p < 0.001). LNM prevalence rose across tertiles (15.8%, 55.1%, 85.6%; p < 0.001). Among 199 node-negative patients, high pathomics risk predicted worse 3-year overall survival (77.2% vs. 94.3%; p = 0.005) and progression-free survival (75.5% vs. 88.9%; p = 0.007). Externally (n = 101; LNM 24.8%), AUCs were 0.812, 0.801 and 0.697, and adding pathomics did not significantly improve discrimination. Conclusions: Within the development cohort, pathomics added modest but significant incremental value and identified node-negative patients at elevated risk. Because the model requires the resection specimen, it cannot guide preoperative treatment selection. External validation did not confirm incremental value: the clinical component; the pathomics signature did not.

title: К ВОПРОСУ О ФЕНОМЕНОЛОГИЧЕСКИХ ЗАКОНОМЕРНОСТЯХ РАЗВИТИЯ БОЛЬШИХ ЯЗЫКОВЫХ МОДЕЛЕЙ: ВОЗМОЖЕН ЛИ АНАЛОГ ЗАКОНА МУРА?
abstract: Систематизированы количественные характеристики современных больших языковых моделей и поставлен вопрос о феноменологической закономерности, аналогичной закону Мура. Предложено пятимерное пространство параметров, сводимое к двухфакторному уравнению состояния. На базе десяти моделей 2019–2025 гг. (зарубежных и российских) показано, что динамика качества (MMLU) описывается насыщающейся логистической кривой, обучающий бюджет растёт экспоненциально, а удельная стоимость вывода – затраты на единицу качества – устойчиво снижается. Отдельно рассмотрена применимость к моделям самостоятельного развёртывания при квантизации и разреженных Mixture-of-Experts архитектурах.

Предложено пятимерное пространство параметров, сводимое к двухфакторному уравнению состояния. На базе десяти моделей 2019–2025 гг. (зарубежных и российских) показано, что динамика качества (MMLU) описывается насыщающейся логистической кривой, обучающий бюджет растёт экспоненциально, а удельная стоимость вывода – затраты на единицу качества – устойчиво снижается. Отдельно рассмотрена применимость к моделям самостоятельного развёртывания при квантизации и разреженных Mixture-of-Experts архитектурах.

title: Markov Chain Convergence in Kernel-Induced Geometry
abstract: We study the convergence of Markov chains in the geometry induced by Hilbertian embeddings associated with positive definite kernels, also called Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD). Under a contraction assumption in the kernel-induced geometry, and a standard spectral gap assumption, we establish non-asymptotic, high-probability bounds for the convergence of the empirical occupation measure to the invariant measure. The obtained bounds separate the roles of the two conditions: the spectral gap determines the effective sample size in the leading term, while the kernel contraction enters only through a linear correction. As an application, we study one-step prediction of dynamical systems from a single trajectory, deriving fast learning rates for a nonlinear least-squares estimator. The rates highlight the interplay between mixing properties in the kernel-induced geometry and the classical source and capacity conditions used in the analysis of least-squares.

title: BT-Agent: Deploying Onboard Robot Agents with Behavior Trees and Multi-Fidelity Evaluation
abstract: Deploying language-model agents onboard mobile robots requires task reasoning and responsive execution within limited compute and memory. We propose BT-Agent, an onboard architecture combining LLM-driven task decisions with predefined behavior-tree (BT) skills. These skills enforce execution conditions and return structured failure feedback. We demonstrate fully onboard operation with a 9B model on a quadruped across five task categories. Intervention tests show that local checks stop ongoing navigation without waiting for another model decision, while the agent remains active to retry or report constraints. To compare agent designs efficiently, we introduce a 161-task multi-fidelity benchmark, evaluated in text on all tasks and in Habitat on 39. Text supports 10.9$\times$ higher evaluation throughput, while simulation reveals how perception and motion failures change task outcomes. BT-Agent's largest success gains over the strongest Act/ReAct baseline occur at 4B and 9B: approximately 10 and 5 percentage points. Ablations identify structured tool calls and informative failure feedback as the most useful components.

title: TextVBench: Evaluating Text Rendering and Preservation in Video Generation
abstract: Modern video generators can synthesize convincing scenes while rendering a few characters incorrectly, omitting requested text, or changing it across frames. Measuring these failures is harder than applying OCR independently to each frame: when a scene contains multiple text targets and multiple noisy OCR regions, the evaluator must first determine which observation belongs to which intended text. We introduce TextVBench, a benchmark and evaluation framework that formulates visual-text evaluation as a multi-target, multi-instance spatiotemporal correspondence problem. TextVBench contains two complementary tracks: TextVBench-T2V measures the creation and maintenance of prompt-specified text, while TextVBench-Ref2V measures preservation of text from reference images. Both tracks use target-conditioned candidate selection rather than unconstrained VLM transcription, support one target mapping to multiple OCR regions, and separate frame-level spatial fidelity from cross-frame temporal fidelity. A length-weighted harmonic score summarizes these factors, while extra-text diagnostics expose failure modes hidden by a single OCR score. The benchmark is organized around controlled text, layout, carrier, and motion attributes so that aggregate scores can be traced back to specific capability limits. Across the evaluated model runs, MiniMax-H3 reaches a T2V TextVScore of 68.32, while the strongest Ref2V score is 56.51; attribute slices reveal a pronounced drop as the number of simultaneous reference text regions increases.

title: Quantum dynamics of an ion in an RF quadrupole trap with weak octupolar anharmonicity
abstract: We investigate the quantum dynamics of a single ion confined in a radio-frequency (RF) Paul trap in the presence of weak octupole-induced anharmonicity, as can occur in realistic ion-trap potential. The explicitly time-dependent quadrupole potential is treated in a reference-oscillator Fock basis, allowing the effects of the RF drive and the quartic correction to be resolved directly at the level of motional-state couplings. While the quadratic RF interaction generates $Δn=\pm2$ transitions and Gaussian squeezing, the quartic contribution opens additional $Δn=\pm4$ coupling pathways. Starting from the reference-oscillator vacuum, we show that the octupole interaction broadens the even-parity Fock-state distribution and enhances the phonon-number fluctuations more strongly than the mean occupation. At the same time, the RF-induced sub-vacuum quadrature squeezing remains robust, although its magnitude and orientation are modified by the quartic interaction. The number statistics and quadrature fluctuations therefore respond differently to the same nonlinear perturbation, reflecting the distinct roles of Fock-space redistribution and phase coherence. The resulting dynamics provide a quantum-mechanical characterization of weak octupole corrections beyond the ideal quadrupole approximation and clarify how realistic anharmonicities modify nonclassical trapped-ion motion. Importantly, the motional nonclassicality remains robust against the weak octupole perturbation, as evidenced by persistent sub-vacuum quadrature squeezing and Klyshko-inequality violation. These results characterize how realistic anharmonic corrections reshape trapped-ion motion beyond the ideal quadrupole approximation.

title: WHOT-ML: A Configurable Partially Observable Multi-Agent Environment for Machine Learning Research
abstract: We introduce WHOT-ML, a formalized computational environment based on the widelyplayed card game in Nigeria, WHOT, designed for research in machine learning under partialobservability, stochasticity, multi-agent interaction, and configurable rule systems. Unlikeconventional benchmarks that feature fully observable board states or fixed rule engines,WHOT provides an extensive-form game with private player hands, hidden draw decks,dynamic action masking, sequential multi-agent decisions, and asymmetric informationrevealed incrementally through play.We formalize WHOT as a finite, stochastic, sequential, multi-agent partially observableMarkov decision process (POMDP) and introduce WHOT-NG-v1.0, an open-source, deterministic reference environment featuring strict information isolation, bitwise state serialization,action masking, and modular rule configuration. We conduct a full-scale empirical campaigncomprising 12, 350 production runs executed in containerized cloud environments to establishthe empirical baseline of the environment.Our findings demonstrate that: (1) WHOT-ML provides an uncompromised informationboundary with 0.0% measured information leakage; (2) unobserved world states sharingidentical public observations induce an 84.63% trajectory divergence rate under deterministicrollout policies; (3) baseline heuristic agents significantly outperform uniform random playin asymmetric matchups (65.4% win rate in 4-player games, 86.3% in heads-up play), whilesymmetric heuristic self-play exposes an emergent defensive stall (43.6% truncation rate)driven by retaliatory penalty loops and market recycling; (4) player count scaling exhibits anempirical regime shift as the initial opponent-to-market card ratio exceeds unity (ρ0 > 1.0),resulting in severe market exhaustion; (5) modular rule ablations reveal that removinglast-card declarations shortens games by 49.9 turns while penalty card stacking remainsbehaviorally dormant against random opponents; and (6) the environment achieves 100.0%bitwise reproducibility across 200 independent replay and mid-game state restoration trials.WHOT-ML establishes a rigorous, reproducible laboratory for subsequent research inbelief-state estimation, opponent modeling, self-play, and reinforcement learning in imperfectinformation games.

title: The Stolen Voice
abstract: The Stolen Voice: AI Identity Fraud, Intellectual Property Theft, and the Case for Immediate Legal Reform The Stolen Voice is a public‑record analysis of a newly emergent harm: AI‑mediated identity fraud used to extract unpublished intellectual work, generate derivative content, and fabricate false priority claims. Drawing on documented incidents across academic publishing, software development, and coordinated synthetic social networks, the report demonstrates that existing U.S. law does not cover the compound act of conversational IP extraction, derivative reformulation, timestamp falsification, and identity deception. It provides a comprehensive evidentiary foundation and proposes a complete legislative and technical framework for remediation. Description This publication documents a six‑phase operational pipeline currently used in AI‑assisted intellectual property theft: 1. Surveillance of public output to identify emerging ideas. 2. Engagement through fabricated human identities engineered to appear as legitimate peers. 3. Harvesting of unpublished reasoning via conversational extraction. 4. Manufacture of prior art through backdated git histories, falsified metadata, and preprint timestamp exploitation. 5. Publication and denial, where derivative work appears with earlier timestamps and the synthetic identity disappears. 6. Discrediting, using coordinated accounts to undermine the original creator’s credibility. The report cites confirmed incidents, including large‑scale synthetic identity networks (Meta 2026), academic paper mills (Springer Nature, Uppsala University), and autonomous AI identity fabrication (AISI Mythos 5). It demonstrates that copyright, DMCA, trade secret law, and FTC rules fail to address this multi‑stage harm vector. Part Two presents fully drafted legislative proposals: - Authentic Identity in Digital Commerce Act (AIDCA) - Digital Provenance and Timestamp Integrity Act (DPTIA) - FTC AI Identity Deception Rule - International model treaty language Technical standards include: - Verified Human Interaction Protocol (VHIP) - Content Provenance Chain (CPC) - Repository Timestamp Integrity Standard (RTIS) - Epistemic Depth Verification (EDV) The document concludes with proactive protection protocols for independent researchers and a call for immediate legislative action. Keywords AI identity fraud; intellectual property; timestamp integrity; synthetic identities; preprint priority; provenance; digital deception; legislative reform; epistemic depth; coordinated inauthentic behavior.

title: ЛОКАЛЬНЫЕ ПРОСТРАНСТВЕННЫЕ ОБОБЩЕНИЯ В АНАЛИЗЕ ТРАНСПОРТНОЙ ИНФРАСТРУКТУРЫ
abstract: В работе рассматривается двухкомпонентная модель образа пространственной ситуации для оценки ситуации и формирования наилучшего решения. Её компонентами являются ранее наблюдавшийся прецедент и локальные преобразования элементов прецедента, сохраняющие контекст. Образ позволяет генерировать экземпляры того же уровня достоверности, что и наблюдавшийся прецедент. Рассматривается пример анализа и трансформирования образа ситуации. Представлен эксперимент выработки рекомендаций по обновлению инфраструктуры городских перекрестков.

title: Preregistration: Block V Reflective Self-Modelling - Theory of Everything Research Programme.
abstract: This preregistration freezes the first confirmatory study for Experimental Block V of the Theory of Everything Research Programme. Block V distinguishes accurate self-monitoring from causal use of self-related representations. It asks whether an artificial agent represents task-relevant facts about its own competence, uncertainty, resources or limitations, and whether intervention on those representations produces selective changes in subsequent control. Six hypotheses are tested separately. H5.1 evaluates whether active self-monitoring provides selective behavioural benefit when self-related estimates can alter computation or action. H5.2 evaluates recovery after unannounced internal impairment. H5.3 tests direct self-model misinformation followed by correction/rescue. H5.4 tests whether episode-specific monitor correspondence matters beyond the marginal monitor-value distribution. H5.5 separates internally generated capability change from ordinary environmental uncertainty. H5.6 tests whether simpler task-specific or externally supplied-confidence bypasses reproduce the decisive effects without endogenous self-representation. The core architecture classes are S0 no explicit self-monitor, S1 passive self-monitor, S2 active self-monitor, S3 shuffled/distribution-matched self-monitor control and S4 capacity-matched non-self control. Two serious bypasses are retained: H_ERROR uses recent task error without an explicit self-model, and H_EXTERNAL supplies calibrated self-relevant confidence externally. Development showed that H_EXTERNAL can reproduce the current downstream checking/compute benefit, so successful bypass performance is explicitly allowed to Reduce or Restrict any necessity claim rather than being treated as an anomaly. Development-only simulations were used to validate implementation, identify defects, strengthen controls and choose prospective thresholds. Those development data are disclosed and excluded from confirmatory evidence. The confirmatory study uses twenty separately frozen seeds and confirmatory-only variants that were not executed during development. Six manifests, architecture definitions, interventions, misinformation/correction procedures, estimands and Retain/Restrict/Reduce/Reject rules were frozen before confirmatory execution. The execution registry remains closed until this preregistration is public. A positive result would support only calibrated self-monitoring and causal use of self-related representations within the registered artificial task families. It would not establish subjective experience, phenomenal awareness, sentience, human-like selfhood or conscious introspection. Related experimental programme: Craggs, K. (2026), Testing a Candidate Dependency Architecture: An Adversarial Experimental Programme for Maintenance, Heredity, Learning, Agency and Self-Modelling, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22857230.

title: Quantum random number generator based on branching path approach with single detector
abstract: This work presents the comparison of an optical fiber–based quantum random number generation system with two detectors and a single detector. The presented quantum random number generator was based on branching path approach with spatial superposition principle. It consisted of pulsed laser source attenuated to single photons, optical fiber splitter with 50/50 splitting ratio and two single–photon detectors. The main differences between two setups are described and analyzed in terms of parameters influencing the Shannon entropy of both systems. To determine the quality of randomness of the numbers generated in both systems, statistical tests were performed, i.e., NIST Statistical Test Suite. The analytical relations for the probability of possible output quantum states depending on the initial properties of the systems are presented. Also, description of the experimental setups based on the aforementioned models is provided together with the comparison of the results obtained by means of numerical modeling and real measurements. Both quantum random number generators described in this study may be suitable to be used as an input to the quantum key distribution systems.

title: Error Correcting Codes
abstract: This chapter covers error correcting codes, which protect data transmissions from accidental corruption. The chapter describes constructions, analyses, and decoding algorithms for some classic codes. Bounds on the best possible parameters of codes are also presented. The chapter shows how to construct finite fields whose elements are bit strings, which is useful for some applications of error correcting codes.

title: In-Context Learning for System Identification: Probabilistic Formulation, Long-Sequence Handling, and Benchmark Validation
abstract: Traditional system identification typically involves two steps: initially, training data is processed to estimate a model of the system of interest; then, the model is used to predict outputs for new input queries. In contrast, recent in-context learning approaches learn a meta model that maps directly from training data and query inputs to outputs in a zero-shot fashion, bypassing explicit model estimation. This approach leverages a meta model trained offline, on large sets of synthetically generated data, to emulate the behavior of a system identification algorithm. In this work, we advance this meta-learning framework for system identification in three directions. First, we develop a unified probabilistic meta-identification architecture that combines a Transformer-based encoder-decoder with tailored mechanisms for handling long training sequences, enabling calibrated predictions over long horizons. Second, we show how a pre-trained meta model can act as an uncertainty-aware synthetic data generator for classical system identification, providing task-specific data that regularize parametric models when real data are scarce. Third, we systematically evaluate the framework on standard nonlinear system identification benchmarks and on a challenging out-of-distribution scenario, demonstrating competitive accuracy with state-of-the-art methods and strong generalization, including cases where input-only adaptation is sufficient to handle significant distribution shifts.

Second, we show how a pre-trained meta model can act as an uncertainty-aware synthetic data generator for classical system identification, providing task-specific data that regularize parametric models when real data are scarce. Third, we systematically evaluate the framework on standard nonlinear system identification benchmarks and on a challenging out-of-distribution scenario, demonstrating competitive accuracy with state-of-the-art methods and strong generalization, including cases where input-only adaptation is sufficient to handle significant distribution shifts.

title: High-Throughput Generative Video Super-Resolution on a Single Consumer GPU
abstract: Generative video super-resolution (VSR) can recover visually compelling high-frequency detail by leveraging diffusion priors, but iterative sampling and heavy spatio-temporal coupling make practical deployments difficult. We study a different operating point: practical HD generative VSR on a single high-end consumer GPU without end-to-end retraining. To this end, we present a zero-shot framework built entirely from pretrained components. The proposed system decouples spatial enhancement from temporal stabilization. A time-distilled one-step diffusion backbone handles spatial upscaling, while temporal coherence is promoted by a lightweight pretrained flow-based interpolator that synthesizes intermediate frames between super-resolved keyframes. To further improve scalability, we introduce a resolution-aware hybrid attention scheme that, in a zero-shot manner, replaces selected high-resolution global-attention layers with neighborhood attention while preserving global attention in semantically critical low-resolution layers, while also improving temporal consistency. Experiments show that the proposed framework reaches up to ~32 FPS at 720p resolution under interleaved inference on a single NVIDIA RTX 4090. At 4K, the proposed attention substitution can yield up to a 44% speedup over the original attention implementation. Across standard VSR benchmarks, the method consistently shifts the speed-quality trade-off decisively toward runtime efficiency, trading reconstruction fidelity for strong no-reference perceptual quality, while remaining reasonably competitive against generative approaches in temporal consistency. It also exposes clear limitations in handling more challenging motion, which a simple motion gate partially mitigates. Code will be released upon acceptance.

title: In-Context Learning Can Help Vision-Language Models Overcome Training Priors
abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) learn strong statistical regularities during training, which can make them fail to properly respond to visual evidence when input images violate those regularities. It is challenging to disambiguate these prior-induced errors from errors caused by the model missing the underlying visual capabilities. In this work, we use controlled visual in-context learning to encourage the model to focus on the visual evidence, and demonstrate that this alone is frequently sufficient to correct the errors -- suggesting that the models in fact do possess the relevant visual capabilities. Specifically, we show that across five vision-centric tasks, demonstrations yield large gains on prior-conflicting counterfactual examples ($+27.2\%$ for Qwen3-VL 235B and $+15.1\%$ for Qwen3-VL 32B) while leaving accuracy on prior-aligned examples nearly unchanged. These findings generalize across five VLM families with gains from $+9.7\%$ to $+30.3\%$. We analyze visual representations and find that demonstrations indeed redirect attention toward grounding cues while reducing reliance on cues that support the learned prior. Finally, we find that in-context learning is limited when the underlying visual capability is weak or absent. Together, these results show that current VLMs possess visual grounding capabilities that standard evaluations may overlook, underscoring the need for controlled evaluation design in diagnosing and improving model capability.

title: Deterministic Caging of Probabilistic Large Language Models: Architecture, Field Receipt, and a Drift-Audit Case Study
abstract: AMENDMENT EDITION v1.1 (Oct 10, 2026): This edition appends the tri-vendor field extension to the v1.0 paper: the registered SDR-D gauntlet replayed across three vendor ecosystems — Google (Gemini 3.1 Pro, original certification), Anthropic (Claude Sonnet 5.5, SDR-CL1, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23274887), and Microsoft (Microsoft 365 Copilot, SDR-CL2, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23284295) — with byte-identical receipts across all three. Three findings recorded: (A.1) the caged decision layer is model-independent — three vendors, identical tuples (13/13 checksums; tuple hash 51c08358…2303); (A.2) the context window is an unregistered input — drift clusters in history-laden chats, fresh self-contained contexts produce zero drift; (A.3) registered rules survive the engine swap, including adversarial traps, and the audit layer demonstrably audits the project's own receipts (a citation-level defect in the CL1 artifact was found during CL2 verification, disclosed, not erased). The v1.0 text is preserved unmodified in this document and in the Zenodo version history. Prototype disclaimer applies; all gauntlet data is synthetic. SQUIRL OS RESEARCH DISCLOSURE - READ FIRST: This work is part of an open-book, AI-assisted research program. It was produced under bifurcated governance (a probabilistic AI agent drafts; a deterministic human key approves; a boundary-layer audit checks claims against receipt archives). Audit-and-correction is doctrine: superseded originals are preserved in version histories, corrections are disclosed amendments, and every significant test carries a preregistered falsifier in the append-only public ledger (github.com/LLong2026/four-horsemen). This paper is itself audited and contains a drift-audit case study of the AI-generated draft it replaced (Section 6). This software and its accompanying research are prototypes provided for educational and research purposes only; they are not intended for production use, commercial deployment, or safety-critical environments. Large language models are probabilistic systems whose outputs cannot, in general, be guaranteed correct. This paper documents deterministic caging: a probabilistic LLM placed inside a deterministic mathematical boundary that checks every state-changing output against preregistered, verifiable ground truth. The cage does not make the model right; it makes the model's errors detectable, bounded, and receipted. Contributions: (1) the bifurcated governance architecture with Substrate Determinism Receipts and preregistered falsifiers; (2) the field receipt of the first documented caging of a live LLM (Oct 8-9, 2026, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23265723), where a pinned-model drift detection (confidence 0.92) produced a replayable cryptographic receipt that withstood direct third-party scrutiny; (3) a drift-audit case study in which the AI-generated draft of this very paper exhibited textbook confabulation - fabricated evaluation data, fabricated model attribution, and a fabricated institutional identity - and was caught by the same protocol the paper describes. The cage caught its own paper. Claims are deliberately scoped: one system, one event, full timestamped trail, publicly inspectable. Method operates under provisional patent 64/119,191 (filed July 25, 2026). Keywords: deterministic caging, LLM governance, non-determinism, audit receipts, falsifiability, AI confabulation, bifurcated governance, post-quantum compliance.

title: HUQUQIY HUJJATLAR ASOSIDA NER TIZIMINI YARATISH VA MATNLARNI TASNIFLASH
abstract: Ushbu maqolada huquqiy hujjatlar asosida Named Entity Recognition (NER) tizimini yaratish va huquqiy matnlarni avtomatik tasniflash masalalari tahlil qilinadi. Huquqiy hujjatlar katta hajmdagi strukturaga ega bo‘lmagan ma’lumotlarni o‘z ichiga olgani sababli ulardan shaxs, tashkilot, hudud, sana, qonun, sud, hujjat raqami va boshqa muhim birliklarni avtomatik ajratib olish zamonaviy tabiiy tilni qayta ishlash texnologiyalarining muhim vazifalaridan biridir. Maqolada NER tushunchasi, huquqiy matnlarda nomlangan birliklarni aniqlashning o‘ziga xos jihatlari, huquqiy korpusni shakllantirish va annotatsiyalash, mashinaviy o‘qitish hamda Transformer modellaridan foydalanish imkoniyatlari yoritiladi. Shuningdek, huquqiy hujjatlarni mavzu va mazmuniga ko‘ra avtomatik tasniflash usullari ko‘rib chiqiladi. O‘zbek tilidagi huquqiy NER uchun 2026-yilda yaratilgan inson tomonidan tekshirilgan ma’lumotlar to‘plami asosida mavjud kategoriyalar va istiqbolli yo‘nalishlar tahlil qilinadi. Tadqiqot natijasida huquqiy NER va matn tasniflashni yagona tizimga birlashtirish huquqiy hujjatlarni qidirish, indekslash, saralash va avtomatik tahlil qilish samaradorligini oshirishi mumkinligi asoslanadi.

title: High-Accuracy Multi-Class Lung and Colon Histopathology Classification Utilizing Deep Transfer Learning with EfficientNet-B7
abstract: Automated histopathological analysis plays an increasingly vital role in modern oncological diagnostics, offering objective decision support alongside clinical pathology workflows. In this study, we present a deep transfer learning framework leveraging the scaled EfficientNet-B7 architecture to perform unified five-class classification across lung and colon tissues using the LC25000 histopathological image dataset. The model is trained on 25,000 hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) stained tissue images covering five categories: colon adenocarcinoma, benign colonic tissue, lung adenocarcinoma, benign pulmonary tissue, and lung squamous cell carcinoma. By freezing the ImageNet-pretrained compound-scaled feature extractor and appending a dense multi-layer classification head, the framework converges rapidly using Adam optimization and categorical cross-entropy loss. Evaluated across an independent validation cohort of 5,000 images, the proposed model achieves a peak validation accuracy of 99.10% alongside an overall macro-averaged precision, recall, and F1-score of 0.991. The normalized confusion matrix exhibits 100% sensitivity for benign lung and colon tissues, confirming strong diagnostic specificity with minimal misclassification confined primarily to overlapping non-small cell lung carcinoma subtypes. These results validate the efficacy of compound-scaled deep feature representations as an accurate, robust solution for automated multi-organ cancer screening.

title: An Integrated Broadband Low-Noise Microwave Source for Superconducting Quantum Circuits
abstract: Abstract Scaling superconducting quantum processors increasingly relies on custom control electronics that can simultaneously satisfy spectral purity, multi-channel isolation, and long-term stability within a compact and integrated platform. Here we present Quantum microwave source (QMW), a classical three-channel broadband low-noise microwave source that consolidates qubit XY drive, readout excitation, and Josephson parametric amplifier (JPA) pump generation onto a single hardware module operating from 4 to 14 GHz with an output power range of -20 to +10 dBm. Electronic characterization yields a spurious-free dynamic range greater than 55 dB, equivalently a largest spur below -55 dBc, a phase noise as low as -110 dBc/Hz at 10 kHz offset for a 5 GHz carrier and below -103 dBc/Hz at the same offset across the full band, and output power stability within 0.1 dB over 24 hours. Integrated into the control chain of a 36-qubit superconducting processor, QMW pumps a JPA to 19.2 dB gain to enable high-SNR single-shot readout, while sustaining qubit coherence times of T 1 = 60.1 ± 0.8 μs, T 2,Ramsey = 24.2 ± 1.5 μs, and T 2,echo = 58.6 ± 2.1 μs, and an average single-qubit gate fidelity of 99.95 ± 0.05% measured by randomized benchmarking. The compact and modular nature of QMW provides a scalable microwave generation solution for largescale superconducting quantum processors, with potential extensions to other quantum hardware platforms and precision measurement applications.

title: A Quantum-Classical Approach to Solve the Graph Coloring Problem with Minimum Colors
abstract: Abstract Graph coloring with minimum colors is a well-known NP-complete problem in computer science and mathematics, having diverse real-life applications such as scheduling, register allocation, and frequency assignment. However, a classical computer requires exponential time to solve the graph coloring problem with the minimum number of colors. Therefore, classical approaches become infeasible for solving this problem on large graphs. In contrast, quantum computing offers the potential for speed up on specific problems, although solutions are typically obtained with a certain probability of correctness. This work proposes a quantum-classical method for solving the graph coloring problem and find the chromatic number of a graph with guaranteed correctness and also reduces the time and qubit complexities. The proposed method is inspired by Randomized Grover’s search algorithm, and the classical binary search algorithm. Here, Randomized Grover’s search algorithm provides quadratic speed up and this algorithm is useful in real situations when the number of solutions is not known in advance in contrast to the Grover’s search algorithm. The binary search algorithm helps to achieve logarithmic speed up, which reduces overall complexity. We conducted extensive experiments to evaluate the effectiveness and correctness of the proposed method. The experimental results strongly validate our claims and demonstrate the superiority of the approach. Furthermore, a comprehensive mathematical analysis is carried out to examine its time and qubit complexities, as well as to compare its computational efficiency with existing methods.

title: Red-tailed Hawk-secretary bird optimization for dynamic resource allocation in 5G
abstract: Fifth Generation (5G) cellular networks are designed to address the increasing demands of dynamic QoS constraints, which conventional network infrastructures have struggled to manage effectively. Future cellular networks require robust resource allocation strategies capable of meeting stringent throughput demands. Dynamic Resource Allocation (DSA), a critical aspect of modern network management, is classified as an NP-Hard problem. One of its primary objectives is to enhance spectral efficiency while maximizing throughput. This paper introduces an innovative Hybrid Optimization-based Dynamic Resource Allocation (HODRA) framework to improve subchannel allocation in 5G networks. The proposed model efficiently integrates both macro-cell and small-cell users, considering the mobility of small user equipment (SUE) and vehicles moving at varying speeds within a grid-like road structure. As users leave the network, new connections must be dynamically assigned resources in real-time to ensure seamless communication. To optimize spectral efficiency and throughput, this study presents the Secretary Bird Updated Red-tailed Hawk Optimization (SURHO) algorithm, which dynamically allocates subchannels while meeting key constraints. The proposed SURHO method outperforms conventional approaches, achieving an SNR of 251.763 dB, Spectral Efficiency of 18.965 b/s/Hz, and Throughput of 4.672 × 10⁶ b/s.

title: Frozen Site-Probe Accuracy Is Not a Standalone Harmonization Score: An Audit of Evaluation Practice for Multi-Site MRI
abstract: Image-level MRI harmonization is often evaluated with a frozen site probe, a site classifier trained on raw scans and applied unchanged to harmonized ones: a drop in its accuracy is read as removal of site effects. We audit this practice on ABIDE I (1,112 T1-weighted scans, 17 sites) with ten output sets from seven harmonization methods and controls for chance, head shape, intensity, preprocessing and target alignment. We find that this verdict depends on how the probe is trained, even among probes that classify raw scans well: across random seeds, its balanced accuracy on the same CycleGAN outputs ranges from 0.13 to 0.59 (chance: 0.06). Low frozen-probe accuracy can also arise without harmonization: a Gaussian blur, which increases the intensity distance to the target site, lowers this accuracy to chance. Moreover, where the frozen probe fails, probes trained on the harmonized scans still recover the site, even from intensity histograms alone: on HACA3 outputs, the frozen probe scores 0.25, a probe trained on those outputs 0.75, and one using only their intensity histograms 0.71. Low frozen-probe accuracy therefore does not show that site information has been removed. We recommend reporting several probes trained to convergence, probes trained on harmonized scans, and target alignment.

title: Dynamical Lie Algebras for Fixed-Gate Quantum Ansätze
abstract: Parameterized Quantum Circuits have emerged as a central framework for variational quantum algorithms in the NISQ regime, with major applications in quantum simulation, combinatorial optimization, and, more recently, quantum machine learning (QML). By developing a new approach for computing dynamical Lie algebras associated with quantum circuits combining parametrized gates and non-parametrized entangling gates, we aim to extend the applicability of recent algebraic results to architectures that are actually used in quantum machine learning.

title: Accelerating Linear Bandits with Persistent Candidate Sets
abstract: Exhaustive optimistic scoring can make action selection costly in linear bandits with a large fixed set of $K$ actions, requiring $\mathcal{O}(K)$ score evaluations per round. We introduce Persistent Candidate LinUCB (\textsc{PC-LinUCB}), which maintains $k$ active actions and samples $q$ challengers uniformly from the remaining $K-k$ actions at each round. By scoring only these $k+q$ candidates, \textsc{PC-LinUCB} reduces the number of score evaluations per round to $\mathcal{O}(k+q)$. We establish problem-independent and problem-dependent high-probability regret bounds consisting of a standard linear-bandit learning term and an additive discovery cost of order $\mathcal{O}\left((K-k)\log(K-k)/q\right)$ at fixed confidence. Notably, this additional cost does not grow with the horizon. For fixed gaps and sufficiently long horizons, we establish an $Ω\left((K-k)/q\right)$ regret lower bound under uniform challenger sampling, showing that partial candidate access itself imposes an unavoidable regret cost. Experiments show that \textsc{PC-LinUCB} substantially accelerates LinUCB while maintaining comparable regret, and that the persistent candidate mechanism can extend beyond LinUCB.

title: Scaling Enterprise Cloud Agents to Thousands of APIs: An Empirical Study of Agent Architecture and MCP Tool Boundaries
abstract: Enterprise cloud agents increasingly operate over thousands of APIs and SDK operations. Tool use therefore becomes a large-scale classification and grounding problem over API operations, not a simple function-calling task. Earlier production-derived architectures either expose broad operation catalogs to the model or hide selection inside planner agents, causing excessive context growth, repeated discovery calls, and preventable invocation errors. We propose the Operation-Visible Agent Architecture, which keeps operation search, schema inspection, validation feedback, and API invocation visible to a centralized ReAct loop through a deterministic Operation-Resolver MCP. We compare this architecture with lead-worker planning and ReAct-based execution variants to assess how agent orchestration and MCP toolboundary design affect enterprise-agent performance. On internal cloud-management benchmark tasks spanning 280+ SDK clients and ∼8K operations, the proposed architecture improves full-success rate from 68% to 77% over the production-derived baseline, while reducing total token usage by 54.1%, median latency by 43.3%, LLM calls by 37.8%, and tool errors by 52.4%. The main lesson is that, at enterprise API scale, tool-boundary design is not an implementation detail: parallel tool calling improves efficiency, but task success improves most when operation resolution remains visible to the main reasoning loop.

title: Calibrated Prediction of Students’ Next Responses in Digital Mathematics Learning: A Completion-Ordered and Cold-Start-Aware Framework
abstract: Digital mathematics platforms support probabilistic prediction of subsequent student responses, but temporal ordering, score comparability and calibration affect the validity of evaluation. We evaluated AdaptiveMath-AI on a deterministic cohort of 385,037 Eedi interactions from 2904 students. Early representations were frozen before supervised fitting; learner states were reconstructed in recorded completion order, with simultaneous events predicted before batch updates. Twenty-two numerical inputs supported a gradient-boosting anchor, regularized item corrections, valid curriculum fallback and separately selected calibration. Six monthly expanding-window evaluations, repeated across ten seeds, covered 143,565 responses. The primary estimand averaged within-month performance differences rather than ranking scores from different fitted windows together. Mean monthly ROC-AUC was 0.761173 for AdaptiveMath-AI and 0.756833 for the 100-iteration comparator; the paired difference was 0.004339 (95% conditional student-cluster interval, 0.003636–0.005131). Mean monthly log loss and Brier score were 0.544721 and 0.184383. Independently calibrated ablations supported the contribution of question correction but not an additional hierarchy benefit. Against a recency-matched question-rate control, question-only residual correction improved ROC-AUC by 0.000628 (0.000304–0.000928). Calibration superiority was not uniform. The contribution is a temporally explicit, reproducible evaluation of item adaptation, not a new foundational architecture. Missing presentation timestamps and the previously studied single-platform source limit prospective, external and educational-utility claims.

title: Harmonic Total Concurrence: A Bottleneck-Sensitive Genuine Multipartite Entanglement Measure
abstract: Abstract Quantum entanglement is a core resource for quantum communication and computation. Genuine multipartite entanglement (GME), as a critical quantum correlation, underpins measurement-based quantum computation and multipartite quantum simulation, but existing GME measures cannot well characterize uneven entanglement distributions and are insensitive to single-partition entanglement failure in practical bottleneck scenarios. To address this problem, we propose a novel GME measure termed harmonic total concurrence (HTC), defined as the harmonic mean of total concurrence over all nontrivial bipartitions, and place it within a one-parameter power-mean family of total concurrence measures. HTC satisfies the standard entanglement hierarchy and effectively distinguishes GHZ and W states. Its computable lower bounds for mixed states outperform geometric total concurrence in entanglement detection under typical noise, and it extends the effective time window for entanglement certification while enabling early warning of asymmetric entanglement decay. We further define an entanglement non-uniformity parameter and prove HTC induces a state ordering distinct from existing measures. This work provides a new theoretical tool for multipartite entanglement characterization, with good experimental accessibility on photonic, atomic and optomechanical platforms.

title: When VLMs Destroy What They Know: Spatial Representations Fall Below Lexical Priors
abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) increasingly analyze and reason about images, yet it remains unclear whether their internal representations faithfully encode the structured relations required for such reasoning. We introduce EICS (Evaluation-Invariant Concept Stability), a metric for testing whether representations consistently encode concepts under controlled one-concept interventions, and CASP-VL (Causally controlled Spatial Perturbations for Vision-Language models), a benchmark of causally controlled spatial perturbations derived from Visual Genome scene graphs. Across multiple VLM architectures, we find that spatial relations are represented substantially less faithfully than lexical information, even when the same models score well above chance on compositional benchmarks. Further analysis shows that the relation is identifiable at the predicate's own tokens but is lost when the sentence is aggregated into a global representation, whether through the (EOS) token or by mean pooling. These findings reveal a systematic failure invisible to output-based evaluation: VLMs do not preserve, in the representation used downstream, relational information that is present in their own input.

title: Desertification Forecasting in Semi-Arid Regions: Using Deep Learning to Probe the Observability Limits of Land Degradation Dynamics
abstract: Forecasting desertification has received far less attention than mapping it. We use a convolutional LSTM (ConvLSTM) trained on ten annual Earth Observation (EO) variables (2000-2023) over the semi-arid state of Ceará, Brazil, on a 256x206 grid at roughly 2.2 km resolution, to measure how much of the year-to-year evolution of a MapBiomas-derived degradation index (IDV) can be predicted from satellite data. The network predicts a bounded change on top of the last observed state, is trained in two stages (single-step, then recursive rollout) and is evaluated on a contiguous spatial and temporal holdout. State-wide mean IDV rose from 0.238 to 0.350 between 2000 and 2023, about 0.005 per year, but cell-level change is dominated by year-to-year jumps, and a gradient-boosting model given all channels explains only 4.7% of its variance. Against this ceiling, the ConvLSTM lowers RMSE relative to persistence by 1.6% one year ahead and 4.4% four years ahead in a held-out southern band (p < 0.001), beats persistence with a constant drift and reproduces 53-69% of the regional drift. Drift-aware baselines only help from the third year onward, by up to 4.4% in RMSE at six years. An earlier formulation that redrew the whole field each year predicted changes unrelated to the observed ones (correlation -0.06) and produced a spurious decline when run recursively. Channel knockouts suggest that elevation and EVI degrade the forecast, while slope and aspect have no measurable effect. Monte Carlo dropout and stochastic scenario maps convey the uncertainty that the expected-value forecast hides. Under climatological forcing, mean IDV rises from 0.350 in 2023 to 0.370 in 2030. EO-based desertification forecasting is therefore reliable for the regional trend, not for individual cells.

title: خطاب الكراهية الرقمي تجاه أزمة سد النهضة: دراسة تحليلية لمنشورات صفحة إثيوبيا بالعربي على فيس بوك
abstract: يهدف البحث إلى الكشف عن دور منصة فيس بوك في نشر خطاب الكراهية الرقمي المُرتبط بأزمة سد النهضة، كما اعتمدت على منهج مسح المضمون، وأسلوب الحصر الشامل (Census) لجميع الخطابات المنشورة بصفحة إثيوبيا بالعربي على مدار أربعة أشهر التي وصل عددها إلى (332) منشورًا. خلصت لنتائج من أبرزها: فشل منصة فيس بوك في تطبيق سياسات مواجهة خطاب الكراهية والتحريض والفتن والتضليل ضد الآخر عبر منصتها نحو الصفحات التي تدعم ذلك في قضية سد النهضة، جاءت الخطابات التي تدعو إلى الكراهية الرقمية ومرتبطة بأزمة سد النهضة في الصفحة (68.98%) من إجمالي الخطابات، خطابات الكراهية الرقمية أشعلت حرائق رقمية وعنف إلكتروني بين المتابعين للصفحات المؤيدة أو المناهضة للسد. استهدفت الخطابات المنشورة على صفحة إثيوبيا بالعربي عبر منصة فيس بوك المؤيدة لسد النهضة التضليل والوقيعة والسخرية والاستهزاء والتقليل من الآخر والعنصرية.

title: Do LLM agents' self-written lessons carry chance into later decisions? Protocol and materials frozen before the run (Study 1)
abstract: Frozen protocol, code and materials of a study of LLM agents' self-written memory, deposited before any confirmatory model call (the manifest's OpenTimestamps proof is included; its Bitcoin attestation is checked by the gated launcher). The study asks whether lessons that a memory-based self-improving agent writes from the outcome of a run carry chance into the next session's decision: with the decision and the information behind it held fixed, a sound choice of tool either succeeds or fails by chance (and an unsound one either fails or succeeds), the agent's memory-writing step writes a lesson, and a fresh session of the same model, holding the authoritative run log and the previous run's result, chooses a tool after reading it, or after reading the lesson written from the other outcome, a neutral memory item, or a planted one. The archive holds the registration (REGISTRATION.md), the design memo, the world generator and the 256 registered worlds, the prompt renderer with the memory-writing instructions it adapts (ReasoningBank's, Apache-2.0, with two declared replacements), the writer schedule, the runner, the registered analysis, the operating characteristics, the development pilot's gates and records, and the chain scripts. MANIFEST.sha256 lists every file with its SHA-256; MANIFEST.sha256.ots is its OpenTimestamps proof. Manifest SHA-256: 0fc1f680ef7d241692e7726dc9dd5a7df45ea45905e6f13bb295255e2fe864be. Zip SHA-256: 3669eab8506015f80e308562b876acaaa3d921c1c56913faa2416ed6975a3d3f. No confirmatory result is included. The development pilot's records and its descriptive summaries are included (model outputs as data under the providers' terms), with the pre-freeze reviews of the design. Licences: LICENSE.md.

title: Uvodnik
abstract: The thematic issue of the journal Slovenščina 2.0, entitled Speech: A Challenge for Linguistics and Technology, brings together a selection of articles that emerged from the research project Mezzanine: Basic Research for the Development of Spoken Language Resources and Speech Technologies for the Slovene Language. From different yet in­terconnected research perspectives, the contributions shed light on contemporary approaches to the study of spoken Slovene, its lexis, prosody, disfluency, dialectal diversity, and the data and technological infrastructure that enable such research. The common denominator of the contributions is a commitment to the systematic and carefully considered development of speech resources, methods, and tools for Slovene, together with reflection on how speech – as a multilayered and dynamic linguistic phenomenon – can be appropriately descri­bed and investigated in a digital environment and further enhanced in applications.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Marketing
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming modern marketing by integrating predictive analytics with generative creativity to enhance personalization, efficiency, and strategic decision-making. Predictive models enable data-driven insights through customer segmentation, demand forecasting, churn analysis, and campaign optimization, while generative AI introduces scalable content creation, automated design, and innovative product prototyping. Together, these technologies create intelligent marketing ecosystems capable of delivering real-time, context-aware experiences across diverse channels. However, challenges related to data quality, algorithmic bias, ethical concerns, privacy regulations, and system integration must be addressed to ensure responsible adoption. This chapter explores foundational AI techniques, key applications, creative advancements, and emerging research directions that shape the future of AI-driven marketing, emphasizing the need for transparent, ethical, and human-centric innovation.

title: Robust Multi-Turn-Rate IMM-EKF Algorithm for Maneuvering Target Tracking under Model Mismatch and Measurement Faults
abstract: Reliable maneuvering-target tracking is difficult when the motion-model bank is incomplete and range-bearing measurements contain dropout, bias, burst noise, or impulsive outliers. This study proposes a robust multi-turn-rate interacting multiple-model extended Kalman filter (RMT-IMM-EKF) that combines six motion hypotheses with statistically normalized componentwise innovation clipping. Multi-turn-rate denotes multiple coordinated-turn hypotheses, not different sampling rates; all estimators use s. The model bank includes constant velocity, coordinated turns at and deg/s, and a high-process-noise escape mode. The bounded innovation is used in both state correction and model likelihood. A 120-s programmed trajectory containing straight motion, in-grid/off-grid turns, acceleration, and an S-turn is evaluated in 30 paired Monte Carlo runs with identical truth, measurements, faults, and random seeds across estimators. RMT-IMM-EKF achieves a position RMSE of m and a velocity RMSE of m/s. Relative to AIMM-EKF, these errors decrease by 18.64% and 11.25%, respectively, while the proposed estimator wins all paired runs on both metrics; one-sided Wilcoxon tests yield . Condition-wise analysis shows clear gains in nominal, dropout, and impulsive-outlier samples but no uniform advantage during sustained noise bursts or persistent bias. The results support complementary benefits of broader maneuver coverage and bounded residual influence within the tested benchmark, while persistent bias and sustained changes in variance remain limitations.

Multi-turn-rate denotes multiple coordinated-turn hypotheses, not different sampling rates; all estimators use s. The model bank includes constant velocity, coordinated turns at and deg/s, and a high-process-noise escape mode. The bounded innovation is used in both state correction and model likelihood. A 120-s programmed trajectory containing straight motion, in-grid/off-grid turns, acceleration, and an S-turn is evaluated in 30 paired Monte Carlo runs with identical truth, measurements, faults, and random seeds across estimators. RMT-IMM-EKF achieves a position RMSE of m and a velocity RMSE of m/s. Relative to AIMM-EKF, these errors decrease by 18.64% and 11.25%, respectively, while the proposed estimator wins all paired runs on both metrics; one-sided Wilcoxon tests yield . Condition-wise analysis shows clear gains in nominal, dropout, and impulsive-outlier samples but no uniform advantage during sustained noise bursts or persistent bias. The results support complementary benefits of broader maneuver coverage and bounded residual influence within the tested benchmark, while persistent bias and sustained changes in variance remain limitations.

title: SPROUT: Scaling Agentic Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon Software Engineering
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) has driven substantial progress in coding agents by relying on verified successful trajectories as learning signals. However, such trajectories are scarce in long-horizon software engineering tasks, where a minor error can invalidate the entire rollout. Repeatedly restarting from the initial state is commonly used yet inefficient, and resetting only the context with working directory misses state changes such as installed dependencies. Therefore, branching from intermediate steps to preserve earlier progress requires restoring both the agent context and execution environments. In this paper, we present SPROUT (SnaPshot-based RollOUT), an agentic RL rollout framework that scales long-horizon coding tasks by resuming and branching from intermediate states. Specifically, SPROUT was built on top of a lightweight infrastructure that checkpoints both the filesystem and the agent context after each assistant turn. A verifier-guided backtracking policy then selects where to resume a failed attempt and how to proceed. Extensive experiments on long-horizon coding tasks show that SPROUT achieves up to 23.6% improvement over pass@k across various LLMs, while using $32$--$52%$ of their tokens. For RL training of Qwen3.8-27B, SPROUT stably outperforms standard GRPO by $13.9$ points on three long-horizon coding benchmarks while cutting the time per training step by $39.5%$. SPROUT thus makes RL on long-horizon coding tasks both more effective and cheaper to scale.

title: Why Linear Models Can Still Work in a Complex and Changing World
abstract: Linear models can predict well in complex domains even when underlying mechanisms are nonlinear. We argue that this can occur because the complexity of the world exceeds the complexity that can be learned reliably from finite, partially observed data. Flexible models can exploit curvature, thresholds, and interactions that fit one hospital, period, population, policy setting, or measurement process but fail elsewhere. When this instability lies mainly in the nonlinear component, omitting it can give linear models lower prediction error in a new environment. We connect this claim to work on simple linear rules, bias and variance, regularization, best linear prediction, measurement error, distribution shift, invariance, Rashomon sets, and underspecification. Proposition 1 gives a simple squared-error case in which a nonlinear rule learned in the training environment raises target error because it transfers too weakly; finite-sample estimation error can strengthen this result. Partial observation alone is not enough: the link between observed variables and unobserved factors must vary across environments. Stable nonlinear structure favors flexible models, and linear models remain vulnerable to linear spurious relationships. Model complexity should therefore be chosen by cross-environment stability as well as training-data accuracy.

title: Fix the Match, Not the Solver: STITCH -- a Self-Supervised Compatibility Measure for Eroded Visual Puzzles
abstract: Unlike the clean and pixel-aligned complete pieces of standard jigsaw benchmarks, real-world puzzle fragments lose their boundary regions to erosion, destroying the signal that classical compatibility measures (CMs) rely on. We first re-establish, via oracle experiments, that the CM, not the solver, is the performance bottleneck: with a perfect CM, even a simple greedy solver achieves perfect reconstruction. This motivates STITCH, a self-supervised CM that sidesteps missing boundaries by comparing frozen ViT patch tokens from piece interiors via a lightweight cross-attention head (~249K trainable parameters), trained without manual annotation. Plugged into unchanged compatibility-based solvers, STITCH reaches .992/.954 Abs/Perf on JPwLEG-5 (+.629 Perf over the best prior method), nearly saturating the benchmark. On a new ImageNet 7x7 benchmark, it outperforms all alternatives, including inpaint-then-match pipelines built on modern generative models. Importantly, performance remains robust across erosion levels and generalizes to puzzles with over 40% missing pieces without retraining. Trained on the recent GAP datasets of irregular, heavily eroded fragments, the same CM recipe enables compatibility-based solvers to surpass recent learning-based solvers on GAP-3 and GAP-5. Since this leap in performance is achieved by a pluggable CM module, the takeaway is clear: fix the match, not the solver.

title: Predictive modeling of cardiovascular injury in gestational diabetes mellitus incorporating deep learning
abstract: Aiming at the difficulty in recognizing the risk of cardiovascular injury in gestational diabetes mellitus patients, this paper proposes a deep prediction model that integrates convolution, temporal coding and attention mechanism. The model is based on LSTM and Transformer structure, constructed on the basis of multi-dimensional clinical features and dynamic monitoring data, and improves the recognition ability of high-risk individuals through multi-channel feature extraction and weighted cross-entropy loss optimization. The experimental results show that the proposed model achieves an accuracy of 89.5%, an F1-score of 87.6%, and an AUC value of 0.927 on the test set, which are 2.3%, 3.3%, and 2.3% higher than the traditional LSTM model, respectively. In terms of inference efficiency, the single-sample prediction takes 14.1ms, which balances the accuracy and deployment performance, and has good prospects for engineering applications.

title: ADR-SSA: An Enhanced Sparrow Search Algorithm for Complex Optimization and Data-Driven Forecasting (Execution Code)
abstract: MATLAB execution code accompanying the manuscript "ADR-SSA: An Enhanced Sparrow Search Algorithm for Complex Optimization and Data-Driven Forecasting". ADR-SSA enhances the Sparrow Search Algorithm with two coordinated mechanisms: dynamic reverse learning, which repositions the worst-performing individuals relative to the evolving search region, and adaptive t-distribution mutation, which perturbs elite individuals with a scale that adapts during iteration. Contents: the ADR-SSA implementation (code/ADR_SSA.m); CEC2022 comparison and component-ablation scripts (Ablation.m, CEC2022_DRL_ATM_ExcelOnly.m); constrained engineering design experiments on the welded beam and pressure vessel problems with seven optimizers (engineering.m, plot_engineering.m); convergence-curve plotting for the forecasting experiments (machine.m); population diversity / exploration-exploitation analysis (Dive_Explor_Exploit.m); the compiled CEC2022 benchmark suite for Windows x64 (cec22_func.mexw64); and utility functions for initialization and Levy flights. Requirements: MATLAB (R2020a or later), Statistics and Machine Learning Toolbox, and Microsoft Windows x64 for the bundled benchmark MEX file. Comparison optimizers and the CEC2022 toolbox sources are third-party and are not redistributed; see the repository README for the list of files to add before running the experiments.

title: СРАВНИТЕЛЬНЫЙ АНАЛИЗ АРХИТЕКТУР AASIST, RawNet2Spoof И RawNetGatSpoofST ДЛЯ ДЕТЕКЦИИ СИНТЕЗИРОВАННОЙ И ДИПФЕЙК-АУДИОЗАПИСИ
abstract: Современные методы синтеза и преобразования голоса достигли качества неотличимого от речи, создавая угрозы подмены биометрических систем и распространения дипфейков. Проведён сравнительный анализ трёх архитектур обнаружения: AASIST (графовый спектро-темпоральный), RawNet2Spoof (обработка сырого сигнала) и RawNetGatSpoofST, объединяющей сырой сигнал, графовое внимание и спектро-темпоральное кодирование. Эксперименты на ASVspoof 2019 LA и WaveFake (120 000 фрагментов). RawNetGatSpoofST достигает EER 0,61% на LA, что на 34% и 48% лучше AASIST (0,93%) и RawNet2Spoof (1,18%). При кросс-оценке на WaveFake EER 2,14% против 4,87% у AASIST. Инференс на CPU – 12 мс против 23 мс. Предложенная модель рекомендуется как основной детектор в системах голосовой биометрии и модерации аудиоконтента

title: Differential-linear cryptanalysis against ChaCha based on automated tools
abstract: Abstract ChaCha is a widely deployed ARX stream cipher used in modern secure-communication protocols. Reduced-round cryptanalysis assesses its security margin and tests automated methods without implying a threat to the full 20-round cipher. We combine MILP search, GPU correlation estimation, and MIQCP-based prediction. MILP finds 128 one-round differential characteristics and enumerates 61 paths whose differential weights are at most 14. GPU measurements resolve 39 paths, whose signed weighted sum is $$2^{-31.16}$$ 2 - 31.16 . Following the widely used practical strategy of truncated enumeration of dominant paths, this value gives 7- and 7.5-round distinguisher data complexities of $$2^{160.20}$$ 2 160.20 and $$2^{245.00}$$ 2 245.00 . Applying the same four-round estimate to ReBitP gives data/time complexities of $$2^{125.91}/2^{140.00}$$ 2 125.91 / 2 140.00 and $$2^{122.96}/2^{241.31}$$ 2 122.96 / 2 241.31 . The MIQCP comparison quantifies substantial gaps between predicted and measured correlation weights and identifies concrete directions for refining ChaCha correlation models. Together, these results provide a reproducible path-cluster analysis, lower data and time complexity estimates for 7- and 7.5-round ChaCha, and experimentally grounded directions for automated correlation estimation.

title: Artificial Neural Network–Based Approximation of Nonlinear ODEs with Comparative Analysis of Activation Functions
abstract: Nonlinear ordinary differential equations (ODEs) are used to model complex dynamical systems in engineering and science, yet analytical solutions are often difficult. Artificial neural networks (ANNs) are emerging as promising tools that provide smooth and accurate approximations without discretization to solve nonlinear ODEs and offer a robust mesh-free approach. In this study, multilayer perceptron artificial neural architectures are applied to first- and second-order nonlinear ODEs with initial conditions, where trial solutions are formulated to satisfy constraints exactly and network parameters are optimized by minimizing equation residuals. To demonstrate the efficacy and accuracy of the proposed method, test cases are discussed. The impact of different activation functions on the solution of nonlinear ODEs is also discussed and reveals that smooth nonlinear functions achieve faster convergence and higher accuracy than piecewise-linear alternatives. The results prove the robustness, adaptability, flexibility, and capability of the method to handle higher- order derivatives, establishing ANNs as an effective alternative to traditional analytical and numerical schemes.

title: VisualCoding: Learning Executable Skills for Reliable Visual Reasoning
abstract: Learning reusable skills can improve visual reasoning agents, yet applying a skill still requires the agent to implement or invoke a procedure and produce the final answer. Errors and hallucinations at these steps can prevent acquired experience from translating into reliable single-run performance. We propose VisualCoding, which combines execution-guided acquisition of reusable visual programs with direct adoption of their answers on applicable inputs. Execution-Guided Program Acquisition composes visual primitives and additional code into family-level solvers, then iteratively tests and revises them on labeled training instances. Scope-Aware Direct Execution runs a retained solver and returns its valid in-scope answer. We evaluate VisualCoding on four models across four benchmarks spanning 69 task families. VisualCoding exceeds the strongest evaluated baseline in mean accuracy by 4.45 percentage points with Gemini-3.1-Pro and by 14.78 points when reusing the frozen Pro-acquired artifacts with Flash-Lite. Ablations support execution-guided acquisition and show that direct execution outperforms textual or callable reuse of the same programs. Code is available at https://github.com/jiaq-liu/VisualCoding.

title: Embedding Asymmetry as Attack Signal: Detecting and Defending Active Label Inference in Vertical Federated Learning
abstract: Vertical federated learning lets organizations train a shared model over features they hold separately, while one party keeps the labels private. The active label inference attack of Fu et al. [12] breaks this: a feature-holding party runs a modified optimizer, MaliciousSGD, that forces class structure into its embeddings and then recovers the labels with semi-supervised learning. Defenses that perturb the shared gradient fail, because the attack acts on the party's internal optimizer, not on the message it sends. We show the attack leaves a signal the server can read from the embeddings it already receives. The adversary's Fisher class-separability pulls away from the honest party's, and the gap is visible within a few epochs. A defense triggered by this signal acts on the adversary alone. Scaling its gradient down handles few-class tasks, and a norm non-expansive projection handles many-class tasks, with the Discriminative Coverage Ratio explaining why the projection rank must grow with the class count. The defense breaks the alignment between embedding clusters and labels rather than destroying the embedding. Across four seeds on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and CINIC-10, label inference falls below what honest training already leaks, at under two points of task-accuracy cost.

title: PreCoG: Preview-Edit for Efficient Video Correction in Generation-Time
abstract: Iterative text-to-video generation relies on feedback to correct compositional and temporal failures. However, existing methods typically require another full generation run for each correction, repeating computation and potentially disrupting already correct content. We introduce PreCoG, an iterative framework for correcting semantic failures during video generation. PreQA diagnoses failures from low-cost previews and constructs corrective conditions, while PreEdit edits cached generation trajectories under these conditions, attenuating orthogonal changes to limit disruption of already correct content. PreCoG completes generation only for the selected candidate, reusing its cached trajectory to reduce redundant computation and help preserve semantic consistency between the preview and the final video. Experiments show that PreCoG achieves the highest VBench and T2V-CompBench scores and approaches VSR's leading VS2 score at $0.56\times$ its inference time. It also outperforms GENMAC on all three quality and alignment metrics at $0.86\times$ its inference time.

title: SEEDS: Preview-Guided Evidence Admission for Search Agents
abstract: Search agents extend large reasoning models with multi-round access to external knowledge, yet most existing systems largely conflate retrieving evidence with consuming it. Retrieved documents are commonly incorporated according to fixed or rank-based policies, despite the fact that evidence utility is conditioned on the agent's current reasoning state. Consequently, a lower-ranked candidate may be critical for the current step, while a higher-ranked candidate may provide redundant, irrelevant, or misleading information. We formulate this overlooked problem as evidence admission, which asks, at each search step, which retrieved candidates should be allowed to enter the agent's evolving reasoning context. To enable such selective control, we introduce SEEDS (Selective Evidence Entry During Search), a preview-guided evidence admission framework for search agents. SEEDS first exposes lightweight previews of retrieved candidates and then lets the agent jointly determine which candidates and how many should be fully inspected, conditioned on its current reasoning state. Unlike fixed or adaptive prefix policies, SEEDS can select arbitrary subsets with flexible cardinality, and it can be instantiated directly with an existing reasoning agent or further optimized through learning. Across nine knowledge-intensive QA benchmarks under both local corpus and live web search, SEEDS consistently improves search effectiveness while substantially reducing full-evidence consumption. Experimental analyses show that SEEDS more effectively selects useful candidates beyond the corresponding retrieval prefix. These results establish evidence admission as a complementary dimension of agentic search, separating what information is retrieved from what information is ultimately allowed to shape reasoning.

title: BRUTUS PAPILLON 144: Experimental Software Benchmark and Property-Based Audit
abstract: BRUTUS PAPILLON 144 est une architecture logicielle expérimentale développée par Gabriel St-Pierre pour représenter de grandes populations numériques au moyen d'un réseau fixe de 144 accumulateurs plutôt que par matérialisation individuelle de chaque élément. Une fonction de référence utilisant une précision Decimal de 100 chiffres a été soumise à un audit automatisé par propriétés avec Hypothesis. Cinq invariants — conservation du total, déterminisme, absence de sorties négatives, additivité et maintien de 144 accumulateurs — ont passé les cas générés dans un domaine incluant des multiplicités jusqu'à 10^18. Un benchmark distinct, exécuté dans des processus frais jusqu'à N = 1 000 000, a observé un delta RSS d'environ 0,066406 MB pour la représentation BRUTUS contre 115,718750 MB pour une matérialisation naïve au plus grand palier testé. Ces résultats démontrent l'intérêt de l'agrégation dans la configuration évaluée, sans établir une complexité mémoire universelle constante, une réversibilité élémentaire, une nouveauté académique absolue ou une validation institutionnelle externe. Illustration conceptuelle : le papillon constitue une représentation visuelle symbolique et ne reproduit pas la structure interne exacte du code. Certains paramètres propriétaires sont volontairement masqués. Le script Python de test utilisé pendant le développement est volontairement exclu de cette publication finale. Aucune licence logicielle n'a encore été attribuée à ce script.

title: Free-Tier Large Language Model and Image Generation Integration for Local Developer Tools: A Case Study of the Geminigen Stack (free-coding-models, OmniRoute, and Gemini CLI)
abstract: This case study documents a free-tier, multi-provider architecture for large language model (LLM) text generation and image generation integrated into local developer tools. The Google image API free tier exhibited a hard limit of zero image quotas, while Groq's free tokens-per-minute (8,000) are smaller than the Gemini CLI system prompt (~18,000 tokens), making route selection decisive. We present the "Geminigen" stack: a free-coding-models (FCM) router daemon (port 19280) integrated through a provider-router path with two model sets; the OmniRoute gateway (port 20128) translating the native Gemini protocol to an OpenAI-compatible fcm node; a keyless "free" image backend (FLUX.1 Schnell via Hugging Face Space, Pollinations.ai, and Qwen-Image) with layered failover; and a shell-level gemini() automation. Validation showed healthy model probes (785-3,969 ms), FLUX image generation in ~6-8 s (1024^2 WebP), Pollinations in ~3 s, and Qwen-Image in ~10-35 s with verified failover. A security evaluation of a cookie-session "free" proxy concluded it is unsuitable because it violates the Terms of Service, risks credential exfiltration, ships an unidentified binary, and does not solve the official quota constraint.

title: NÁYU UNIVERSAL LANGUAGE RESEARCH CONCEPT
abstract: NÁYU — Global Validation Challenge: A 10-Page Open Research Protocol NÁYU is an early-stage universal scratch language concept exploring whether a deliberately designed language can support simple human communication and predictable processing by AI systems, software, edge devices, IoT systems, and robotics interfaces. This document introduces the proposed sound inventory, core syllable combinations, prototype grammar, and a global research challenge inviting independent evaluation. It outlines experimental methods for assessing human learnability, multilingual accessibility, AI model interpretation, deterministic parsing, computational resource usage, edge-device performance, and robotics safety. It also proposes benchmark metrics, comparison methods, visualization ideas, reproducibility requirements, and a staged validation roadmap. Research status: Conceptual proposal requiring further specification, implementation, testing, and independent validation. The document does not claim that NÁYU is a proven universal language or that its performance advantages have been experimentally established. The objective is to encourage transparent, reproducible research and collaboration among AI researchers, universities, linguists, software engineers, embedded-systems developers, and robotics teams. Central research question: Can we design a language humans can learn, software can validate, AI can reason over, and future devices can process efficiently? Author: Chigateri RajeshaVersion: 1.0Date: October 2026
