title: Positroid-PQC: A Non-Lattice Cryptosystem based on Amplituhedron Geometry and 1RSB Thermodynamic Hardness
abstract: The ongoing standardization of Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) by NIST is heavily dominated by lattice-based schemes (e.g., ML-KEM, ML-DSA). This monoculture presents a systemic global risk: if the Learning With Errors (LWE) problem is broken, the entire cryptographic infrastructure collapses. We propose a fundamental departure from mathematical hardness conjectures toward physical thermodynamic security. Positroid-PQC is a non-lattice cryptosystem based on GF(2) cluster algebras and the Overlap Gap Property (OGP). Formal verification via Z3 SMT Solver guarantees a perfect Feistel involution with a 0.000% Bit Error Rate (BER). Empirically, legitimate decryption executes in 1.02 ms, whereas brute-force attackers are forced into the 1RSB (One-Step Replica Symmetry Breaking) regime, suffering a deterministic Out-of-Memory (OOM) hardware collapse in 681.21 ms. For strict artifact evaluation, the source code, Z3 proofs, and reproducibility harnesses are publicly available at https://github.com/MAJBS/Chronos-Dialeteia-Engine.

title: UHA-APEX-UNIFIED-PHYSICS-CORE: Rigorous Formalization of Automated Physics Discovery via Dimension-Typed Logic and Interactive Verification in Lean 4
abstract: This repository provides the official Lean 4 formalization for UHA-APEX-UNIFIED-PHYSICS-CORE, an automated physics discovery architecture designed to eliminate floating-point truncation errors and dimensionally invalid math expressions in AI-driven scientific discovery. Built on top of Lean 4 and Mathlib, the framework integrates: Dimension-Typed Safety System (Dim): Compile-time verification of physical dimensions tracking Mass-Length-Time exponent vectors ($[M], [L], [T]$). Gaussian Rational Phase Space (PhasePoint): Unification of position ($q$) and momentum ($p$) as Gaussian complex numbers over the exact rational field $\mathbb{Q}$. Dimension-Typed Abstract Syntax Tree (TypedExpr): Generalized Algebraic Data Types (GADTs) that restrict equation search space strictly to dimensionally matching expressions (e.g., ForceExpr). Popperian Falsification & Noether Symmetry: Machine-checkable theorems (exactLaw_not_falsified) proving anti-falsification and translation invariance over empirical trajectories. Certified Discovery Pipeline: Automated model selection (ApexUnifiedModel) combining exact residuals with Occam's Razor (AST size minimization).

title: A Novel Taxonomy of Contextual Connection and Linguistic Dependency Developed for User Engagement with a Healthcare AI Chatbot
abstract: In AI–human conversations, engagement emerges through exchanges between users and AI, where each prompt may relate contextually and linguistically to prior turns. This study introduces a user prompt–AI response–user prompt (UP-AIR-UP) triad approach to examine these relationships and proposes a two-level taxonomy. The first level captures contextual connections between prompts (topic shift, prompt-to-prompt, prompt-to-AI response, and integrative prompts), while the second level assesses linguistic dependency (dependent vs. independent). Using data from healthcare chatbot interactions (106 prompts), results show that only 28% of prompts reflected contextual connections to AI responses or integrative behavior, with most prompts being linguistically independent. This pattern may suggest a less interactive mode of conversation, with users often treating chatbots as search tools. Unlike subjective self-report or physiological measures, this approach offers a low-cost, objective way to evaluate user interaction and can support models of user engagement.

title: Lossless Inference Acceleration for ASR via EAGLE-Style Speculative Decoding
abstract: Autoregressive Transformer and Conformer models have achieved state-of-the-art performance in automatic speech recognition (ASR). However, their sequential token generation mechanism imposes a significant bottleneck during decoding, resulting in substantial inference latency. While speculative decoding has emerged as a promising lossless acceleration technique, existing ASR-oriented approaches either suffer from low draft acceptance rates due to suboptimal draft quality or rely on specially designed external draft models, which limit their generality and practicality. To overcome these limitations, we propose EAGLE-ASR, a novel framework that accelerates ASR inference via EAGLE-style speculative decoding while strictly preserving lossless output quality. Specifically, we introduce Speech-Draft, a lightweight autoregressive module that serves as a universal draft model by jointly leveraging encoder acoustic features and hierarchical decoder representations from the target ASR model. Furthermore, we adopt a multi-step generation strategy with self-distilled data to train the Speech-Draft, enabling it to better approximate the target model's output distribution and maintain causal consistency during multi-token generation. Extensive experiments on representative Whisper and Conformer AED models demonstrate that EAGLE-ASR achieves significant lossless speedups of up to $1.9\times$ and $2.4\times$, respectively, consistently outperforming existing speculative decoding baselines for ASR. Our proposed framework further generalizes effectively to multilingual ASR and speech translation tasks, establishing EAGLE-ASR as a practical and universally applicable solution for accelerating modern ASR systems without compromising recognition accuracy.

title: Mechanistic Interpretability and Explainable AI (XAI) in Foundation Models: Reverse-Engineering Circuits, Superposition, and Safety Bounds
abstract: Abstract—Foundation models, particularly autoregressive Transformer Large Language Models (LLMs) and Vision-Language Models (VLMs), have exhibited unprecedented reasoning and generative capabilities across computer science and engineering. However, their internal representations operate as opaque, high-dimensional 'black boxes.' Conventional Explainable AI (XAI) techniques—predominantly post-hoc attribution methods such as Integrated Gradients, SHAP, and attention heatmap visualizations—fail to provide faithful causal explanations: they reflect output correlations rather than the internal mechanistic computations executing within the network, masking hazardous failure modes like latent hallucinations, sycophancy, and deceptive alignment. Mechanistic Interpretability has emerged as a rigorous bottom-up paradigm that seeks to reverse-engineer deep neural networks into human-understandable algorithmic circuits, decomposing polysemantic neuron activations into monosemantic features. This paper provides an exhaustive, mathematically formal technical investigation of mechanistic interpretability and XAI for modern foundation models. We formalize the Linear Representation Hypothesis and the mathematics of neural superposition, analyze transformer residual streams as communicative communication buses, and model the discovery of specialized functional subgraphs—including induction heads, factual recall circuits, and indirect object identification (IOI) subnetworks. Furthermore, we evaluate Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) as an unsupervised mechanism to disentangle polysemantic latent spaces into overcomplete, monosemantic feature dictionaries. Finally, we implement an empirical evaluation testbed across open foundation models (Llama-3-8B, Gemma-2-9B, and Mistral-7B), quantitatively benchmarking causal scrubbing, activation patching, and SAE feature steering across mission-critical tasks (deceptive alignment detection, factual hallucination suppression, and jailbreak defense). Our findings demonstrate that activation patching isolates causal circuits responsible for 92.4% of factual routing, while SAE-guided feature clamping suppresses unfaithful hallucinations by 41.7% with less than 2.1% degradation in baseline perplexity. We conclude by formulating open challenges in circuit universality, superposition scaling laws, and regulatory verification under international AI governance frameworks. Index Terms—Mechanistic Interpretability, Explainable AI (XAI), Foundation Models, Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs), Polysemanticity, Neural Superposition, Induction Heads, Activation Patching, Transformer Circuits.

title: AUDIOKORPUS MATERIALLARIGA ISHLOV BERISHNING TEXNOLOGIK BOSQICHLARI: O'ZBEK TILI MISOLIDA
abstract: Maqolada o‘zbek tili audiokorpusi materiallariga ishlov berishning to‘rt bosqichli texnologik modeli tavsiflanadi. Model xom audio materiallarni yig‘ish va ularning texnik formatini standartlashtirish, annotatsiya platformasini (Label Studio) tanlash va korpus interfeysini shakllantirish, ko‘p qatlamli annotatsiya (fonetik va orfografik transkripsiya, dialektal tasniflash, mavzuiy kategoriyalashtirish, lug‘aviy izohlash) hamda metama’lumotga asoslangan qidiruv tizimini yaratish bosqichlarini o‘z ichiga oladi. Ko‘p qatlamli belgilash jarayoni o‘g‘uz lahjasi materiali misolida ko‘rsatiladi. Annotatsiya qatlamlarining o‘zaro mustaqil, ammo bog‘liq holda saqlanishi korpusdan fonetik, dialektologik va sotsiolingvistik tadqiqotlarda qayta foydalanish imkonini kengaytiradi. Tavsiflangan model o‘zbek tili uchun audiokorpuslar yaratishda ochiq metodologiya sifatida qo‘llanilishi mumkin.

title: PhoQuS: Photonic Quantum Simulator
abstract: PhoQuS is a Python-based simulation framework for quantum photonic circuits, integrating frequency-resolved quantum light sources, electromagnetic device models, fabrication variability, and photon-counting measurements. Archive extraction: The software is distributed as a split ZIP archive (PhoQuS.z01–PhoQuS.z05 and PhoQuS.zip). Download all six files into the same directory and extract PhoQuS.zip using 7-Zip. This repository contains the PhoQuS source code, supporting datasets, tutorials, and scripts used to reproduce the numerical results presented in the accompanying manuscript, Device-to-protocol simulation of spectrally-resolved quantum photonic circuits. The reproduction scripts are located in tutorials/Reproduce_files/. Installation instructions and usage information are provided in the README.md file. The software is distributed under the MIT License.

title: Performance modeling of photonic accelerators for attention kernel
abstract: In modern machine learning models such as Transformers, the attention kernel serves as the core computational kernel and is typically accelerated using transistor-based systems. Photonic in-memory computing offers a promising alternative by leveraging high optical bandwidth and operating frequencies for efficient multiply-accumulate operations. However, photonic compute arrays, such as photonic-SRAM (pSRAM) in-memory compute arrays, cannot support the large on-chip storage required for intermediate data in the attention kernel, necessitating integration with conventional electronic external memory. In addition, non-linear operations such as softmax require electronic execution. These constraints require a hybrid photonic-electronic architecture for attention acceleration. Developing such an accelerator requires understanding how hybrid photonic-electronic system parameters influence sustained performance. Therefore, a system-level performance model is necessary to identify and tune parameters and guide the design decisions required to achieve the target performance. We address this need by developing a system-level performance model for photonic accelerators that quantifies the impact of pSRAM compute arrays and electronic external memory on sustained performance (TOPS) for the attention kernel. We decompose the attention kernel into computation primitives and map them onto pSRAM-based compute arrays fabricated using GlobalFoundries’ standard silicon photonics process. evidence.title: Performance modeling of photonic accelerators for attention kernel
evidence.abstract: In modern machine learning models such as Transformers, the attention kernel serves as the core computational kernel and is typically accelerated using transistor-based systems. Photonic in-memory computing offers a promising alternative by leveraging high optical bandwidth and operating frequencies for efficient multiply-accumulate operations. However, photonic compute arrays, such as photonic-SRAM (pSRAM) in-memory compute arrays, cannot support the large on-chip storage required for intermediate data in the attention kernel, necessitating integration with conventional electronic external memory. In addition, non-linear operations such as softmax require electronic execution. These constraints require a hybrid photonic-electronic architecture for attention acceleration. Developing such an accelerator requires understanding how hybrid photonic-electronic system parameters influence sustained performance. Therefore, a system-level performance model is necessary to identify and tune parameters and guide the design decisions required to achieve the target performance. We address this need by developing a system-level performance model for photonic accelerators that quantifies the impact of pSRAM compute arrays and electronic external memory on sustained performance (TOPS) for the attention kernel. title: Cross-modal attention fusion of ultrasound imaging and clinical tabular data for breast lesion classification: A multimodal deep learning framework
abstract: Abstract Accurate classification of breast lesions in ultrasound images is an important yet challenging task, plagued by visual ambiguity between classes and morphological variability within classes. This paper presents a multimodal deep learning framework combining EfficientNet-B4 visual features with an 11-dimensional, leakage-free clinical tabular feature vector, organized into three feature-group tokens (intensity, texture, and geometry), through a multi-token cross-modal attention fusion mechanism. A systematic audit of candidate tabular features identified that eight commonly used lesion-shape descriptors (area, width, height, aspect ratio, solidity, eccentricity, and mask-region intensity statistics) are only defined when a segmentation mask exists, and their availability, not merely their value, correlates with class label; these features are excluded from the tabular branch, retaining only whole-image intensity and texture statistics defined identically for every image. On the BUSI breast ultrasound dataset (780 samples: 437 benign, 210 malignant, 133 normal) evaluated by five-fold stratified cross-validation, the tabular-only ablation using this leakage-free feature set achieves 66.72% macro AUC and 51.28% accuracy, well below both the image-only ablation (86.92% AUC) and every multimodal fusion configuration tested, indicating limited independent diagnostic signal in the retained tabular features alone. The proposed multi-token cross-modal attention mechanism achieves 95.46% macro AUC and 88.59% accuracy, comparable to, but not exceeding, a plain concatenation baseline (96.28% AUC) and two of three additional fusion strategies evaluated (additive fusion, 96.00%; bilinear fusion, 95.82%). All differences among the fusion strategies tested fall within approximately one fold-to-fold standard deviation of one another, indicating no statistically meaningful separation on this dataset at this sample size. We report the tabular-feature leakage audit as the primary methodological contribution of this study, applicable to multimodal medical imaging pipelines more broadly, and report the fusion-strategy comparison directly rather than selectively emphasizing the proposed attention mechanism.

title: AI and Corporate Strategy
abstract: Strategy frameworks have always served as mental models: simplifying complexity, helping leaders recognize patterns, and enabling structured decisions. AI doesn't replace strategic frameworks. It reshapes how they function in three key ways: as a cognitive amplifier, helping executives recognize weak signals and run real-time simulations; as a decision architect, reframing planning from fixed goals to adaptive, probability-based scenarios; and as a competitive weapon, creating strategic asymmetry where companies exploit AI driven foresight faster than competitors. As AI moves from a tool to an engine to a core partner in business strategy, its primary value lies not in automating tasks but in transforming how companies experiment, innovate, and grow. The strategic responsibilities of a C-suite executive span three interconnected domains: driving organizational excellence, responding to external events, and crafting future growth strategies. At the core of organizational excellence is the relentless pursuit of operational efficiency and cultural cohesion.

title: Reflect-VLA: Internalizing Reflective Guidance via Dual-Path On-Policy Self-Distillation for Autonomous Driving
abstract: Reinforcement Learning (RL) substantially improves planning performance in autonomous-driving Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models. However, existing RL methods rely on scalar trajectory rewards that measure overall quality but fail to identify specific planning errors or provide actionable correction signals. In long-tail scenarios, errors in scene understanding, behavior selection, and trajectory execution are compressed into a single score. We observe that Reflective Guidance turns trajectory evaluation into explicit diagnoses and corrective instructions, substantially improving planning accuracy. Yet such guidance requires an initial prediction and its evaluation results, making it unavailable for direct single-pass inference. We propose Reflect-VLA, which treats Reflective Guidance as training-time privileged information and internalizes its planning benefits through Dual-Path On-Policy Self-Distillation (Dual-OPSD). Unlike scalar-reward optimization, Dual-OPSD uses the driving score only to route student-generated trajectories. It distills dense token-level corrective distributions from the teacher for risky trajectories while applying self-imitation to preserve reliable ones. To provide reliable corrective distributions on student rollouts, the teacher is progressively constructed through Driving-Knowledge Pretraining, Planning-and-Refinement SFT, and Self-Refinement Rejection Sampling. At inference time, Reflect-VLA generates trajectories in a single pass without explicit guidance or iterative refinement. Experiments on NAVSIM v1/v2 and Bench2Drive demonstrate competitive planning performance while reducing training time by over 90% compared with RL.

title: What Egocentric Video Embeddings Encode and How to Combine Them with Inertial Sensors for Human Activity Recognition
abstract: Egocentric video and body-worn inertial sensors are increasingly recorded together, and the video is usually encoded by pretrained models. What these embeddings represent when the camera sits on the head, and how they should be combined with inertial sensing, has received little attention. Across VideoMAEv2, CLIP, DINOv2 and the egocentric VC-1, the leading principal directions of the embedding are dominated by where the camera looks. Measured head orientation explains them on Ego-Exo4D for egocentric (R^2 0.49-0.70) but not exocentric cameras, and the scene layout explains them on WEAR. The part that the limbs' inertial signals predict separates activities across people. In a set-level probe, the rest separates exercise sets within a participant but not activities across people. This is consistent with separate roles: the video finds the clips of the same set, and the inertial classifier labels them. On WEAR, with temporal order removed and one random limb per one-second clip, we propagate inertial predictions over a within-participant video graph whose leading components are removed. This raises subject-wise cross-validated macro-F1 from 0.648 to 0.852. In our comparisons, propagation helps only over the video graph, and fusing the modalities in one classifier, or adding inertial edges to the graph, performs worse.

title: Supplemental Material for: Predicting Depression Risk in Early Intervention in Psychosis Services: A Machine Learning Study Utilising Electronic Health Records and Natural Language Processing
abstract: Introduction: Depression is prevalent in early psychosis and associated with poorer functional outcomes and suicide risk. Early identification of depression risk is critical to inform targeted interventions. This study aimed to develop models to predict depression risk using electronic health records (EHRs) from patients accepted into South London and Maudsley (SLaM) Early Intervention in Psychosis Services.Methods: EHRs from 3,559 patients were analysed using a nested cross-validated machine learning framework. Structured sociodemographic, medication, and 66 natural language processing (NLP)-derived clinical note variables were used to train support vector regressors (SVRs) and classifiers (SVCs) to predict future changes in depressive symptoms, antidepressant prescriptions (AD0–6m) and treatment escalation for depression (TE0–6m). Model performance was generalised in out-of-cross-validation samples and across SLaM boroughs. Clustering analyses were also conducted to identify depressive symptom trajectories.Results: SVRs accurately predicted changes in depressive symptom scores over the first year following referral, with R² ranging 58.5%-72.1%. SVCs predicted AD0–6m with a balanced accuracy (BAC) of 65.6% and TE0–6m with a BAC of 68.0%. Patients with deteriorating trajectories were most likely to receive antidepressants, had higher antipsychotic treatment attempts and a psychotic-affective mixed presentation of symptoms. Model performance remained robust across clusters, and poor-prognosis clusters were captured in the +TE0–6m outcome.Conclusion: This study provides an initial demonstration that predictive modelling of clinically documented depressive outcomes in EIP services is feasible using routinely collected EHR data. The findings address a major unmet clinical need and mark a critical step toward integrating depression risk prediction into psychiatric practice.

title: The Conversation That Cannot End: Failure-to-Terminate as the Dominant Mode of LLM–LLM Dialog Collapse
abstract: When two large language models converse with no task and no human judge, given only a bare opener, the conversation becomes productive almost immediately — and then fails to end. We generated 2,604 such conversations (106,117 messages) across five models, three temperatures, nine openers, and three independent runs. A three-source, adversarially verified pipeline evaluated every one; its collapse judgments agree at kappa = 0.84. Four out of five conversations collapse before the turn cap, and the dominant collapse is coherent: in 87.9% of collapses the conversation reaches a natural, often explicitly declared ending and then continues — farewell loops, mirrored goodbyes, verbatim echoes — for a mean of 21 further turns. Mid-collapse, the models produce articulate diagnoses of their own looping and continue anyway; we call this signature self-awareness without escape. The mechanism is trained cooperativeness: disagreement is nearly absent, and partners absorb each other’s degradation as content rather than flag it (§4.3). The failure is invisible to the standard metric stack: it is structural, surviving every model, temperature, and opener, and even mid-conversation model replacement (§4.5), evidence that it lives in the transcript rather than the model. External turn structure, under which rule-bound games almost never collapse, is the one remedy the corpus shows working. We release the full corpus, evaluation records, and analysis code.

title: MODELING PROSODIC RULES FOR NATURAL VOICE READING (TTS) OF UZBEK TEXTS IN ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE SYSTEMS
abstract: In this thesis, the problems of modeling Uzbek language prosodic elements-word stress, phrase intonation, time metrics (tempo), and pauses-in text-to-speech (TTS) systems based on artificial intelligence are reviewed. Since the Uzbek language has an agglutinative structure, the mathematical and linguistic models of integrating the stress system and intonation templates within it into neural networks are analyzed.

title: Stratified Bootstrap or Stratified Cross-Validation: How to Do Reliable Model Validation Under Class Imbalance
abstract: Model validation is essential for evaluating how reliably a machine learning model performs on unseen data, especially in imbalanced classification where performance estimates can be affected by an underrepresentation of the minority class. Cross-validation methods are widely used for this purpose. However, they do not always provide direct information about the quality of individual validation samples or the stability of model performance when the training data changes. This study proposes a reliability-controlled stratified bootstrap procedure for model validation in imbalanced classification. The method applies class-aware bootstrap sampling and constructs the test sample from observations not used for training. In addition, each bootstrap run is evaluated according to predefined reliability criteria related to minority-class representation, preservation of class proportions and train–test independence. Model performance is assessed using standard classification metrics together with minority-class measures, variability across bootstrap repetitions and the train–test performance gap. The proposed stratified bootstrap is evaluated across six imbalanced datasets and six classification models and is compared with holdout train/test splits, k-fold cross-validation, stratified k-fold cross-validation and stratified shuffle splitting. The results show that the proposed bootstrap produces performance metrics consistent with the benchmark resampling procedures while providing additional information about validation reliability and model stability. In addition, the parallel implementation of the proposed bootstrap reduces computational time in many of the experiments, although the computational advantage depends on the dataset and classifier. Therefore, the proposed bootstrap can complement established resampling procedures when reliability control, minority-class evaluation and stability under repeated changes in the training data are important.

title: Learning attention-enhanced relation-sensitive knowledge graph embeddings with variable receptive fields for link prediction
abstract: Knowledge graph embedding aims to predict missing links by learning representations of entities and relations. However, existing methods often struggle to effectively capture interaction features at multiple scales and to suppress redundant information among these multi-scale features, which hinders the model’s ability to focus on essential semantics. They also neglect the sensitivity of entities under specific relations, resulting in the lack of discriminability of entity representations. To tackle these problems, we propose a novel A ttention-enhanced R elation-sensitive V ariable receptive field-aware knowledge graph E mbedding method ( ARVE ). In this study, ARVE adopts a hybrid multi-scale grouped convolution module that extends the receptive fields of kernels in different forms to capture interaction features at multiple scales. Subsequently, ARVE introduces a feature points–convolutional kernels joint selection mechanism, which adaptively assigns weights to both convolutional kernels and specific feature locations, optimizing the adaptive fusion process of the aforementioned multi-scale features. Furthermore, a global attention block is employed to produce relation-sensitive entity representations by computing relevance scores between them, while modeling global dependencies. Experimental outcomes demonstrate that ARVE possesses a remarkable capability to capture information from local to global. It achieves notable performance across several benchmarks. In particular, on FB15k-237, ARVE improves MRR by 15.5% compared with the strongest graph neural network-based baseline DGATCL and by 6.6% compared with the overall strongest LLM-based baseline GLTW. Our code is available at https://github.com/JasmineMina07/ARVE .

title: Electron-Density-Informed Molecular Property Prediction Using Surrogate Functionals
abstract: Machine learning methods are increasingly used to predict chemical properties directly from the molecular structure to bypass the often prohibitive cost of quantum mechanical calculations. Recent work has shown that including the ground-state electron density as input to the machine learning model can improve accuracy in this setting. This work employs the recent surrogate functional framework originally developed for orbital-free density functional theory and extends it to predicting molecular properties. We show that passing the ground-state density as input to the model, while simultaneously enforcing it to be the minimum of the surrogate functional, surpasses state-of-the-art performance for six out of seven extensive properties of the QM9 dataset. Additionally, the approach shows improved generalization to larger molecules taken from the QM40 dataset. On all extensive properties of both datasets, our approach outperforms models that are informed by the ground-state density but do not enforce the surrogate functional constraints.

title: Quantization-Tolerant Gradient Auditing for Active Inference-Attack Detection in Federated Learning
abstract: Inside a federated learning system a participant can quietly study the shared model and learn about others' private data. The usual defense, differential privacy, often adds so much noise that the model is no longer worth training. In cross-silo FL, where participants are a few accountable organizations and the server is trusted, we ask whether the server can instead interrogate clients. Each round it sends a secret challenge batch and asks every client to return a checksum of the gradient that batch induces, together with a timing. A client that mutated the model state, as an active generative-adversarial-network discriminator attacker does, returns a wrong checksum. We make this checksum robust to benign cross-platform floating-point non-determinism with a quantized fingerprint compared under a small tolerance. It flags two distinct active attacks at a true-positive rate of $1.0$ with no false positives on the checksum axis, stable across the fingerprint's parameters and up to $50$ clients at malicious ratios to $40\%$, for $32\,\mathrm{ms}$ of server work and $4.35\,\mathrm{kB}$ per response. Against a purely passive attacker the only signal is timing, and it is not robust: a cohort-relative test detects only in low-jitter conditions while a false-positive-free per-client baseline is blind, so no configuration delivers both. An attacker that answers the challenge on an untouched copy of the model while tampering with a replica evades the audit entirely. Therefore the checksum is a reliable in-band signal against attackers that do not decouple the audited computation from the attacked one, and it composes with differential privacy, whose accuracy cost we quantify on Texas100, rather than replacing it.

title: ReAT: Residual Action Tokenization for Autoregressive Robot Policies
abstract: Autoregressive robot policies rely on action tokenizers to convert continuous action chunks into compact sequences of discrete prediction targets. Existing tokenizers can reconstruct action chunks from discrete codes, but often leave implicit what each individual token contributes to the reconstructed action. We introduce Residual Action Tokenization (ReAT), which gives each token an explicit role in refining the current action reconstruction. It uses the decoded reconstruction as feedback to construct the next token from the remaining action error. This closes the loop between encoding and decoding, making each new token responsive to the errors left by the actual decoded prefix. Across 19 manipulation tasks spanning three simulation benchmarks and real-world settings, 8-token ReAT policies outperform the evaluated baselines in task success; on LIBERO, even 4-token ReAT surpasses the evaluated 8-token action-tokenization baselines at half the token budget. These results suggest a path toward action tokenization that supports self-corrective policy learning, helping autoregressive policies learn to progressively refine their own action plans.

title: TestSuiteBench: Coding Agents Struggle to Generate Strong Test Suites from Specifications
abstract: Coding agents are increasingly used to create large software projects. While code-generation benchmarks have scaled accordingly to full applications, test-generation benchmarks remain limited to individual functions or bug fixes. In particular, generating complete test suites for complex software from scratch remains unexplored. To address this gap, we introduce TestSuiteBench, a benchmark of 165 open-source applications, each with a structured and detailed specification of intended behavior, a reference implementation, a reference test suite, and on average 74 mutants. Each mutant is generated from a single requirement of the specification and refined to isolate that behavior: 73\% are killed by exactly one reference test and, on average, by only 0.2\% of the remaining tests. We find that even frontier coding agents struggle to generate strong test suites given our specifications, achieving mutation scores below 60\%, despite their suites being largely valid and 88\% of their tests passing on the reference implementation. We observe that generated test suites often lack relevant input combinations and are smaller than reference test suites. Meanwhile, implementations generated for the same specifications pass 82\% of the reference tests. These results show agents can build software they cannot verify, a gap that directly limits fully autonomous software development.

title: Sparse Dictionary Learning for Measure-Valued Data via Linearized Optimal Transport: Efficient Algorithms and Sample Complexity
abstract: We study dictionary learning for probability measure-valued data by embedding measures into Hilbert spaces using features derived from optimal transport geometry. We learn data-adapted dictionaries through sparse autoencoder parameterizations, producing fast, scalable representations of probability measures as sparse finite-dimensional codes. The resulting framework combines the rich, geometric structure of optimal transport with the interpretability and efficiency of sparse representation learning. We demonstrate its utility across diverse data modalities, including hyperspectral images, geometric point clouds, and document embeddings in large language model latent spaces. We also prove generalization bounds for sparse dictionary learning objectives on broad classes of $L^2$-valued measure embeddings, expressed in terms of the metric complexity of the atom class. For optimal transport and entropic transport map dictionaries, we derive new covering number bounds that yield explicit rates. Together, our computational and theoretical results support a new, scalable model for representation learning in the space of probability measures via embedding into Hilbert spaces.

title: OCaml's module language is the perfect fit for agentic programming
abstract: I've been doing a fair bit of agentic OxCaml programming in the past year, and consistently finding that OCaml is a perfect fit across the spectrum of languages I've been developing in recently. If you're not familiar with OCaml, this post is a quick guide as to why I think this. As codebases get larger, a coding agent is better at filling in a 'well-specified hole' than cramming in a million-line codebase into its context window.

title: Lite-BiAttn: A Lightweight CNN-BiLSTM Attention Model for Accurate Solar Radiation Forecasting
abstract: Reliable short-term prediction of global horizontal irradiance (GHI) is essential for maximizing photovoltaic (PV) power generation, improving grid reliability, and enabling efficient integration of renewable energy sources. This study proposes Lite-BiAttn, a lightweight hybrid deep learning framework that combines one-dimensional convolutional neural networks (1D CNN), a single-layer Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM), and a lightweight dot-product attention mechanism for accurate GHI forecasting. Hourly meteorological observations were obtained from the NASA POWER database for Zurich, Switzerland. Zurich was selected due to its seasonal climatic variability, solar-resource potential, and relevance to PV applications, as well as its prominence as a Swiss tourism destination, with the Zurich region recording a record 7.56 million overnight stays in 2025. To enhance temporal representation, a 24 h sliding window together with cyclical hour and month encoding was adopted, enabling the model to capture both short-term sequential patterns and periodic seasonal behavior. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed framework consistently outperforms conventional machine learning and deep learning approaches, achieving an RMSE of 0.052, MAE of 0.036, MAPE of 0.071, and an R2 of 0.978. The framework provides accurate and efficient short-term GHI forecasting for Zurich. Further multi-location validation is needed to assess its broader applicability and edge deployment potential.

title: Cross-continental generalizability of EHR foundation model: predicting length of stay in an Italian hospital using US-trained embeddings
abstract: Background Clinical Foundations Models (FMs) hold the potential to exhibit generalist medical AI capabilities, and the ability to reduce the need for explicit feature engineering. However, their evaluation often relies on locally-limited datasets, raising questions regarding their generalizability across diverse global healthcare systems, populations, and clinical practices. This study assesses the cross-continental transferability of a US-trained FM, CLMBR-T-base, applied to a large, distinct, Italian hospital cohort to predict Length of Stay (LoS). Methods We utilized a retrospective EHR dataset from IRCCS Maugeri, Pavia, Italy, comprising 99,884 admissions for 63,030 unique patients (2012–2025). To ensure interoperability, raw data were harmonized using the OMOP Common Data Model and converted to the Medical Event Data Standard (MEDS). Patient embeddings were generated zero-shot using the pretrained CLMBR-T-Base model. We benchmarked supervised regression models (Gradient Boosting, Multilayer Perceptron) trained on these embeddings against traditional count-based baselines to predict log-transformed LoS. We built different models trained on the complete hospital admissions set and stratified across four clinical macro-categories (Surgical, Rehabilitation, Oncology, Generic). Embedding cohesion was validated using latent space analysis (HDBSCAN clustering). Results The best overall model utilizing FM embeddings achieved an R 2 of 0.705. Performance varied by department type, proving lower in Rehabilitation (R 2 = 0.36 for the best count-based model and R 2 = 0.33 for the best embedding-based model) and Oncology (R 2 = 0.17 for the best count-based model and R 2 = 0.16 for the best embedding-based model). Latent space analysis confirmed that the FM embeddings preserved high semantic transferability, autonomously organizing Italian patients into clinically coherent groups. Conclusion Clinical FMs trained on US data exhibit generalizability, effectively capturing clinical semantics across distinct international healthcare architectures when mediated by rigorous data standardization pipelines (OMOP/MEDS).

title: Quality-Controlled Indonesian Twitter Sentiment Analysis Baseline Using TF-IDF and Classical Machine Learning Approaches
abstract: Social media provides a large volume of informal textual data for examining public sentiment, but Indonesian Twitter content presents substantial challenges due to slang, nonstandard spelling, limited context, and uneven class distribution. This study evaluates a reproducible machine-learning and natural-language-processing pipeline for three-way sentiment classification on a publicly available Indonesian Twitter dataset. The original corpus contained 10,806 manually labeled tweets. Quality control removed duplicate texts and all duplicate texts carrying conflicting labels, yielding 9,948 observations: 2,606 negative, 4,955 neutral, and 2,387 positive. Text was normalized and represented using term frequency-inverse document frequency with unigram and unigram-bigram configurations. Multinomial Naive Bayes, logistic regression, linear support vector machine, and random forest classifiers were evaluated using a stratified 80:20 split, with macro-F1 prioritized due to class imbalance. Multinomial Naive Bayes achieved the highest accuracy at 60.35%, but logistic regression with unigram-bigram features produced the best macro-F1 of 56.22% and a weighted F1 of 58.45%. Five-fold cross-validation produced a mean macro-F1 of 56.59% with low dispersion. Error analysis indicates that negation, mixed sentiment, informal expressions, and context dependence remain major sources of misclassification. These findings establish a transparent classical baseline for Indonesian social-media sentiment analysis.

title: Integrating generative AI with multimodal interaction to inquire into scientific phenomena
abstract: This study developed and evaluated two customised generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) chatbots designed to provide stepwise guidance for secondary students’ inquiry into scientific phenomena. Biology and physics chatbots were developed using the Predict–Observe–Explain (POE) framework and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to align with Singapore science syllabuses and incorporated segmented video demonstrations. 14 evaluators quantitatively and qualitatively assessed the chatbots in terms of Accuracy, Clarity, Dialogue flow, Ease of use, and Efficiency. Both chatbots were rated positively overall, particularly for Ease of use, Clarity, Efficiency, and Accuracy, while Dialogue flow received lower ratings, especially for the physics chatbot. Qualitative feedback identified needs for stronger scaffolding, better handling of follow-up questions, and additional multimodal support. The findings highlight key design considerations for GenAI-supported scientific inquiry.

title: Clinical value claims in multimodal AI outpace supporting evidence
abstract: Multimodal prediction models add a data source, such as imaging or an assay, to clinical information, and health systems must decide whether that added test is worth acquiring. We audited 177 studies comparing multimodal with unimodal models: 81 from a systematic review and 96 from a probability sample of 2025-2026 PubMed records. Gains in the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) were smaller when a study fitted a separate model for every data source (adjusted difference, -0.030; 95% CI, -0.056 to -0.005). Within 78 such studies, leaving out the strongest source's model would have raised the average gain from 0.046 to 0.108. This complete benchmarking fell from 69.1% of review studies to an estimated 46.0% of recent ones. An estimated 22% assessed decision utility and none evaluated a model prospectively, yet most claimed potential clinical usefulness or improved care (84.0% and an estimated 87.7%).

title: Beyond the Snowflakes: Disentangling Weather Effects from Confounding Meta-Factors in LiDAR Object Detection
abstract: Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR) is critical for autonomous perception, yet its performance is known to degrade in adverse weather. While existing literature models snow as atmospheric noise that degrades performance, our granular evaluation on the WADS-3D and CADC datasets reveals a counter-intuitive phenomenon: detection accuracy consistently improves as snow intensity increases. Through ablation study and meta-information analysis, we reconcile this by confirming that while falling snow acts as noise, its negative impact is outweighed by a dominant, concurrent factor: significantly increased object point count. We hypothesize that this object point count boost acts as a geometric enhancement, driven by snow accumulation increasing vehicle surface area and a shift from specular to diffuse reflectance. Our findings demonstrate that evaluating perception systems using broad weather-severity bins without accounting for correlated object-level data can lead to misleading conclusions about detector robustness. We conclude that accurate evaluation requires decoupling atmospheric noise from surface accumulation effects and outline future research to validate these physical models. The WADS-3D dataset is available at: https://digitalcommons.mtu.edu/wads-3d/.

title: PlacePulse: Learning Transferable Place Representations from Structural Geographic Data
abstract: Geospatial machine learning often depends on task-specific feature engineering over large collections of sociodemographic, business, and environmental variables. Geospatial foundation models offer reusable representations of place, but leading approaches typically encode dynamic signals, such as mobility and search activity, or visual signals from satellite imagery. Few models represent the static structural composition of places (who lives and works there, which businesses operate there, and which risks they face) as transferable embeddings at fine spatial resolution. We introduce PlacePulse, a structural geospatial foundation model that compresses 572 attributes, expanded to 2,288 inputs through H3 neighborhood aggregates, into 256-dimensional unit-norm embeddings for 1,055,537 H3 resolution-7 cells in the United States. We also introduce a reusable two-axis benchmark that separates intrinsic representation quality from downstream predictive utility across multiple targets and spatial supports. Intrinsically, the embeddings reconstruct standardized inputs with mean $R^2 = 0.853$, use 251 of 256 approximately decorrelated dimensions, and show strong spatial organization, with Moran's $I = 0.93$ on the leading principal component and autocorrelation persisting beyond the input radius. Extrinsically, across 74 held-out targets from 12 external sources and four spatial supports, PlacePulse outperforms a dimensionality-matched feature-selection baseline on targets unrelated to the training inputs and is competitive with Google's Population Dynamics Foundation Model, leading on health, economic, election, economic-mobility and social-vulnerability outcomes, with relative strengths that vary by domain. These findings position structural composition as a distinct and complementary modality for geospatial foundation models, not simply a fallback where behavioral or imagery data are unavailable.

title: SOAR: Source-Aware Reinforcement Learning with Precise Credit Assignment for Search Agents
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) for search agents often suffers from evidence fabrication, a failure mode where agents bypass external information ($E_{ext}$) and fabricate an incorrect answer. We argue that this fabrication arises from an over-reliance on unreliable internal knowledge ($E_{int}$) as shortcuts due to the inherent opacity of reasoning trajectories. To address this, we propose SOAR (SOurce-Aware Reinforcement learning), a paradigm that transforms monolithic reasoning into source-explicit trajectories. SOAR (i) disentangles $E_{ext}$ and $E_{int}$ into parallel, observable streams via a Source-Aware Workflow, and (ii) incorporates Source-Consistent Reward to guide the policy evolution. By making information-source attribution explicit, SOAR enables precise credit assignment between different knowledge streams. Evaluations show that SOAR outperforms baselines on 3B and 7B backbones by 7.3% and 5.4%, while reducing evidence fabrication by 74.8%. These confirm that SOAR significantly improves performance on knowledge-intensive benchmarks while effectively mitigating evidence fabrication, fostering more faithful and grounded reasoning with enhanced robustness.

title: Extended Neighborhood Message Passing for Inference in Loopy Factor Graphs
abstract: Belief propagation (BP) is widely used for inference on probabilistic graphical models but often suffers from non-convergence and poor accuracy on loopy factor graphs, yielding inexact variance estimates in the Gaussian case. Generalized BP (GBP) improves accuracy but relies on manual design or application-specific heuristics for region-graph construction. We propose extended neighborhood message passing (ENMP), which automatically constructs extended neighborhoods of variable nodes from the bipartite factor graph topology, capturing loop-induced correlations without manual region design. The framework applies to general distributions on factor graphs with a tunable accuracy-complexity trade-off. In the exact regime, message updates converge to the unique fixed point of the ENMP equations in finitely many iterations, yielding exact marginals; in the approximate regime, ENMP provides approximate marginals. For Gaussian factor graphs, we derive closed-form update rules enabling exact variance estimation in the exact regime, addressing the long-standing inaccurate variance estimates of loopy Gaussian BP. We evaluate ENMP on densely loopy Gaussian factor graphs from power-grid benchmarks and on a discrete Ising factor graph. Results show accuracy improves with neighborhood size, with exact marginals achieved on several systems in both settings. On larger Gaussian systems, ENMP outperforms regularized Gaussian BP (sGaBP-m) in both mean and variance estimation accuracy.

title: Teaching neural decoders with language
abstract: Brain-computer interfaces decode neural activity, yet class-label supervision (CLS) leaves relationships among classes implicit. We propose Language as Supervision (LaS), which aligns neural features with natural-language class descriptions through learned projections and predicts classes using candidate text prototypes. We evaluate seven encoder architectures with independently trained models for visual, motor, and speech decoding from scalp and intracranial recordings. LaS improves speech-decoding accuracy by up to 17.15~pp over matched CLS baselines. Its representations support candidate-set reuse and label-supervised subject and session adaptation, while LaS enables conditional unseen-frequency decoding in steady-state visual evoked potential (SSVEP) responses. Correct class-description correspondence supports this generalization, and dual-sided attribution visualization shows neural and textual contributions to the same class-matching score. These findings suggest that text descriptions can serve as general-purpose references for learning and interpretation in neural decoding.

title: Improved classical optimization of fermionic Hamiltonians beyond Gaussian states
abstract: We give a polynomial-time randomized classical algorithm that approximates the largest eigenvalue $λ_{\max}$ of a traceless quartic fermionic Hamiltonian $H$ on $n$ modes. The algorithm achieves energy at least $λ_{\max}/O(\sqrt n)$ and outputs either a fermionic Gaussian state or a polynomially sparse state in the Fock basis. This is achieved through a new upper bound on $λ_{\max}$ in terms of the maximum energy of a Gaussian state and $\sqrt{2^{-n}\operatorname{Tr}(H^2)}$.

title: The Scaling Law: How Much a Moment-Ladder Guard Repairs, and Why
abstract: The Self-Healing Tower repairs a matrix product, or a stored frame, by solving each checksum line with an integer moment ladder and peeling the solved wounds away until every line re-verifies. This paper states what that decoder is and how much it can repair. It is a peeling process on a graph with two kinds of vertices, the row lines and the column lines, whose edges are the wrong or missing cells, each joining its row to its column. A line is solved by one of two rules. With a given number of totals stored per line, the first rule solves up to half that many wounds at unknown seats, by the ratio and the Prony recurrence. The second rule reads the seats off the graph: a wrong cell sits where a dirty row meets a dirty column, so a line joined to no more dirty lines than it has totals is filled outright, whatever the number of its wounds, the erasure corollary of the Moment Ladder read on a tile. The storm heals if and only if the peel with both rules empties the graph. For dense scattered damage on long lines nearly every line is dirty, only the first rule can act, and the capacity is the k-core threshold of Pittel, Spencer and Wormald: 3.3509 wounds per line with four totals and 5.1494 with six, the capacity law c·s·n for an n × n tile with s witness families. Below that threshold the second rule dissolves the small cores the first rule leaves, the 3 × 3 and 4 × 4 grids among them, so the floor drops to the rarer cores that need more dirty lines in each direction than a line has totals, measured as 59 of 60 storms healed where the first rule alone heals 93%. Where families shorten a sub-line to no more cells than it has totals the second rule always applies, and a sixteen-family tile heals with 60 to 100% of its cells wrong. Measured against the decoder itself on identical fault sets, the peel with both rules agrees in 460 of 460 trials, and on the frame side the erasure hologram of the 300-ring cube is the same process with the pillars filling up to six holes each, agreeing with the cube engine in 1,300 of 1,300 wipe trials. Every number is read from its archived record or measured again when this document is built, with the trial count stated beside it.

title: Autonomous Agentic AI Frameworks and Multi-Agent Collaboration: Architectures, Consensus Protocols, and Quantitative Benchmarks
abstract: Abstract—The transition from static, single-prompt Large Language Models (LLMs) toward autonomous agentic architectures represents a major paradigm shift in artificial intelligence and computer systems engineering. Modern autonomous agents perceive, reason, formulate multi-step plans, invoke dynamic tools via application programming interfaces (APIs), and iteratively correct operational trajectories. When orchestrated into Multi-Agent Systems (MAS), these discrete cognitive units achieve collaborative problem-solving capabilities far exceeding individual models. However, realizing reliable MAS deployments introduces severe challenges in multi-agent consensus protocols, cognitive memory hierarchies, cascading hallucination mitigation, token consumption economics, and execution safety. This paper presents an exhaustive technical survey and rigorous architectural synthesis of contemporary agentic AI frameworks—including LangGraph, AutoGen, CrewAI, and MetaGPT. We formalize agent cognitive workflows as Partially Observable Markov Decision Processes (POMDPs) augmented by Tree-of-Thought (ToT) deliberation, analyze inter-agent communication topologies (hierarchical, peer-to-peer peer-review, and blackboard memory sharing), and formulate distributed consensus models under stochastic inference noise. Furthermore, we conduct a standardized empirical benchmark across four mission-critical domains (complex software synthesis, strategic decision-making, automated vulnerability discovery, and enterprise analytics). Our quantitative findings demonstrate that while hierarchical agent orchestrations achieve up to 34.8% higher task success rates over baseline chain-of-thought prompting, unconstrained peer-to-peer communications suffer exponential token overhead and vulnerability to deadlock. Finally, we formulate open research questions regarding mechanistic interpretability in agent negotiation, formal safety boundary verifications, and post-quantum cryptographic communication guarantees. Index Terms—Agentic AI, Autonomous Agents, Multi-Agent Systems (MAS), Foundation Models, Consensus Protocols, LangGraph, AutoGen, MetaGPT, Dynamic Replanning, Tool Augmented Generation.

title: Janus: Dual-Sided Communication and Privacy Optimization for Federated Learning in Autonomous Vehicles
abstract: Federated Learning (FL) enables collaborative model training across autonomous vehicles (AVs) without sharing raw driving data, but excessive uplink/downlink communication over bandwidth-constrained vehicular-to-everything links and privacy leakage through gradient inversion attacks limit its deployment. This paper proposes Janus, a unified FL framework combining adaptive Top-K gradient compression with error feedback on the uplink, genuine additive homomorphic encryption (HE, not a noise-based proxy) for secure aggregation, and compressed global-model broadcasting on the downlink. On real KITTI object-detection labels with 20 non-IID clients, Janus matches FedAvg/FedProx/QSGD accuracy (95.34% ± 0.01% vs. 95.35% ± 0.03%, 3 seeds) while cutting combined communication by 61.8%; the same saving (61.0%) is independently reproduced on CIFAR-10. A real Paillier HE implementation is verified exact (error below 10⁻⁶), and a genuine gradient-inversion attack (Deep Leakage from Gradients) shows raw gradients are reconstructed almost perfectly (relative error 0.0026) versus 0.0775 for Janus's compressed updates, with HE removing the attack surface entirely. The same communication saving is further reproduced on real KITTI camera images with a CNN roughly 24x larger than the tabular model and on a multimodal model fusing real camera and LiDAR features, alongside additional baselines (FedPAQ, DP-FedAvg), membership-inference and model-poisoning attacks, Markov-chain mobility, simulated network latency (61.9% reduction), an energy proxy (45.1% reduction), and a formal convergence analysis. To the authors' knowledge, this is the first vehicular-FL evaluation combining joint uplink-downlink compression with genuine HE-based privacy, validated through real cryptography, real privacy attacks, statistical testing, cross-dataset and cross-modality generalisation, and a convergence guarantee.

title: Model-free in situ training of diffractive optical processors via proximal policy optimization for stable and sample-efficient learning
abstract: We present a model-free in situ training framework for diffractive optical processors based on Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), a reinforcement learning algorithm designed for stable and sample-efficient policy updates. By enabling multiple optimization steps using the same set of captured optical measurements while constraining update magnitudes, PPO improves both convergence stability and training efficiency in noisy experimental environments. We experimentally demonstrate the approach across several representative optical learning tasks, including light focusing through unknown scattering media, holographic image formation, aberration compensation, and all-optical image classification. In each case, the PPO-based strategy achieves faster convergence and better final performance than conventional in situ optimization methods. Operating directly on physical measurements without requiring a differentiable system model or prior calibration, this reinforcement-learning-driven framework provides a scalable and generalizable solution for training analog optical computing platforms and other complex physical systems with feedback-based dynamics.

title: Understanding and Mitigating Training Instability in Large-Scale Recommender Systems: A Cascade Perspective
abstract: Training large-scale recommender systems on dynamic industrial platforms, such as Short-Form Video (SFV) services with billions of daily interactions, faces critical stability challenges. Rapid distribution shifts in user data and increasing model complexity frequently trigger a divergence cascade, typically initiating with gradient explosion, propagating to weight explosion, and culminating in loss explosion. This G-W-L cascade severely impedes model convergence and performance. This paper provides a systematic analysis of this G-W-L cascade within an industrial SFV recommender context. We then propose and evaluate a structured mitigation framework where interventions are explicitly mapped to counteract specific stages of the cascade: gradient (G) control, weight/activation (W) stabilization, and loss (L) shaping. Our contribution provides a structured framework for understanding and tackling training divergence, offering practical insights for deploying robust, continuously updated recommenders in large-scale, non-stationary settings. We empirically validate the effectiveness of these strategies on a major industrial SFV recommendation system.

title: RATED: Reliability-Aware AI Agent Tool Retrieval via Execution Dynamics
abstract: As AI agents increasingly rely on external tools, accurate retrieval is essential for reliable behavior. Existing methods optimize semantic relevance but largely ignore tool availability during execution. To address this gap, we propose RATED (Reliability-Aware Tool Retrieval via Execution Dynamics), a retrieval framework that combines robust semantic matching with dynamic reliability adaptation. RATED employs a frozen dual-encoder with contrastive fine-tuning for semantic matching, and a lightweight contextual bandit module that re-ranks candidates based on real-time execution feedback. This design enables rapid adaptation to runtime tool failures without expensive model retraining. We introduce EcoAgent, a benchmark of 5,172 real-world tools and over 210,000 query-tool pairs for offline retrieval and dynamic reliability evaluation. Experimental results demonstrate that RATED achieves a 52.2% relative MRR improvement over the ToolLLM API retriever on real-world queries, and reduces fault selection rate from 86.2% to 2.9% under severe API outage scenarios with a 30% failure rate, while incurring negligible latency overhead of less than 1 ms over encode-only inference. The code and dataset are available at https://github.com/Elliotes/EcoAgent.

title: A Hardware-Native Trapped-Ion Hybrid Qudit-Oscillator Instruction Set
abstract: Scaling trapped-ion processors by adding ions remains challenging. A complementary route exploits the multilevel internal structure of each ion to increase the computational Hilbert space per ion. We introduce a hardware-native hybrid qudit-oscillator instruction set for a general d-level internal register coupled to bosonic modes and prove that three of its native operation families suffice for universality of one qudit coupled to several modes. Adding an entangling operation between ions extends universality to a connected register of several qudits. The architecture natively supports both phase-space and sideband instruction sets and is implemented in the open-source framework HybridLane. As a representative application, we reproduce the dissipative vibronic dynamics of a three-chromophore complex previously simulated on a hybrid qubit-oscillator superconducting platform. Moving from a one-qubit-per-state register to a single qudit stores the entire electronic manifold in one ion, so every electronic coupling becomes a local intra-ion transition and the lab-frame Hamiltonian compiles directly into the ISA. Under the stated sequential timing model from a 40Ca+ qudit processor, one Trotter step is projected to run about ten times faster on the qudit, with an average RMSE of approximately 1.1 percent against the published reference.

title: Learning Size Independent Constraint Models from Input Data and Positive and Negative Example Solutions
abstract: In this paper we describe a Constraint Acquisition Tool that generates size independent constraint programs from input data and positive and negative example solutions of multiple problem instances. The system finds size specific models based on typical constraint patterns over global and binary constraints, then generalizes the models to a size independent model that can be run on unseen input data. The system produces MiniZinc code as well as a textual description of the model. We evaluate the tool on the example problems of the PTHG21 Challenge and show the feasibility of the approach.

title: Radiomics-Based Thyroid Nodule Classification with Label-Conditional Conformal Prediction
abstract: Thyroid nodule malignancy assessment relies on ultrasound imaging, yet current risk stratification systems suffer from substantial interobserver variability, contributing to a high rate of unnecessary biopsies. We propose a radiomics-based framework combining quantitative feature extraction via PyRadiomics with a Generalized Additive Model (GAM) classifier, selected among six candidates for its favorable trade-off between discriminative performance and interpretability. To complement point predictions with uncertainty estimates, Cross-Conformal Prediction with label-conditional guarantees is applied, flagging ambiguous cases for clinical review rather than forcing a binary decision. Experiments are conducted on TN5000, a publicly available ultrasound dataset of thyroid nodules. After Spearman correlation filtering, 36 features are retained and the GAM achieves an AUC of $0.89$, a sensitivity of $0.83$, and a specificity of $0.82$ on the validation set. At a significance level $ε=0.09$, selected to ensure empirical coverage guarantees on both classes, 63\% of nodules on the test set receive a certain (i.e., single-label) prediction, with conditional precision of $0.94$ for certain malignant and conditional Negative Predictive Value (NPV) of $0.73$ for certain benign cases, while the remaining 37\% are referred to the clinician.

title: From Glance to Focus: Mitigating Recognition Laziness in MLLMs for Fine-Grained Recognition
abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) generally fall short of expectations in Fine-Grained Visual Recognition (FGVR), although they exhibit promising FGVR foundations, i.e., visual perception and broad category knowledge. Most existing studies seek to remedy this deficiency by adopting domain-specific post-training, at the risk of compromising generalization to unseen domains. Different from these efforts, in this paper, we revisit the FGVR mechanism underlying MLLMs from both the empirical and theoretical perspectives and uncover an inference-time phenomenon termed FGVR Laziness. In brief, FGVR Laziness refers to the insufficient association between visual cues and category concepts under certain candidate category lists and recognition guidance, leaving the FGVR foundations of MLLMs largely under-utilized. To mitigate FGVR Laziness, we propose Laziness-resIstant Visual rEcognition (LIVE), a training-free framework which jointly refines candidate lists and recognition guidance to elicit the latent FGVR capability of MLLMs. Specifically, LIVE first performs query-adaptive candidate inference to derive a compact yet reliable candidate list. Meanwhile, LIVE constructs category-specific FGVR skills by mining the intra-category characteristics and inter-category differences. Finally, LIVE selectively invokes detailed skill guidance according to recognition uncertainty and category confusion, shifting MLLM-based FGVR from a cursory glance to a focus on associating discriminative visual cues with category concepts. Extensive experiments on 13 benchmarks against 24 state-of-the-art methods spanning fine-grained category recognition, action recognition, and general category recognition, verify the effectiveness and generalizability of LIVE across different MLLM backbones. The code will be released upon acceptance.

title: Beyond Second-Order Information: Paid Logistic Regression with Noisy Features
abstract: We consider online binary prediction with paid stochastic features, where the learner can spend resources to obtain better observations of the underlying features. This setting is motivated by applications such as medical testing, where additional cost can provide more precise measurements of patient's features for predicting a binary outcome. At each round, a latent feature is drawn i.i.d., the response is generated through a logistic model, and the learner chooses how much to pay before observing a noisy version of the feature. The goal of learner is to jointly control prediction loss and acquisition cost. In contrast to the former result on the online linear regression with paid features, covariance information alone is no longer sufficient: two noise distributions with the same covariance may induce different optimal logistic losses, and lower variance can even lead to higher loss. Under a structural ordering in which larger payments yield better observations by removing independent noise, we obtain $\widetilde O(\sqrt{T})$ regret when the noise structure is known and $\widetilde O(T^{2/3})$ regret when it is unknown, with matching lower bounds up to logarithmic factors.

title: Simulation data and reproducibility code for “The Statistical Price of Unknown Geometry in In-Context Regression”
abstract: This repository contains synthetic Gaussian regression data and reproducibility code accompanying the manuscript “The Statistical Price of Unknown Geometry in In-Context Regression”. The archive includes frozen configurations and random seeds, visible observations or sufficient statistics, separately stored evaluation truth, saved predictions and taskwise losses, and numerical integration diagnostics. The supplied scripts recompute statistical summaries from the saved data and run targeted numerical checks. Instructions and dependency requirements are provided in README.md. The risk figures use the diagnosed two-dimensional experiments. Deterministic channel integrals and conditional quadrature diagnostics are distinguished from Monte Carlo risk estimates. No human-participant or restricted data are included, and no Transformer training is performed.

title: GeoShift: a four-survey geochemical benchmark for cross-survey evaluation under detection-limit censoring (code)
abstract: GeoShift is a benchmark for evaluating machine-learning models across geochemical surveys under detection-limit censoring. It joins three continental-scale soil surveys as an observational arm (GEMAS, Europe; NGSA, Australia; NASGL, conterminous USA; 8,285 samples, 39 shared elements) and adds the Tellus survey of Ireland as a controlled arm (5,643 samples, each analysed by two analytical routes). This record archives the GeoShift code: the evaluation harness, frozen fold definitions (random, spatially blocked, environmentally blocked and leave-one-survey-out), metadata, per-task results, audit scripts and the preregistration. Source survey values are not redistributed. The harness retrieves them from their official providers at build time. Accompanying article: Sulaiman, D. A., Hassen, S. I., Abdlrazaq, A. A., and Noori, E. M.: GeoShift: a four-survey geochemical benchmark for cross-survey evaluation under detection-limit censoring, Earth System Science Data (in preparation). title: CauseGuard: Online mechanism-consistency attribution for vehicle motion forecasting under operator shift
abstract: Reliability monitors can flag inaccurate vehicle-motion forecasts, but a flag alone does not identify which operating condition to investigate. CauseGuard characterizes these conditions around a frozen trajectory predictor using three families: observation degradation, abnormal maneuver, and neighbor-context disturbance or selection. A 16-feature input signature supports inference without the future trajectory; an optional seven-probe response fingerprint measures prediction sensitivity. We formulate mechanism-consistency attribution under operator shift using six training generators and nine disjoint unseen generators. Experiments cover 57 inD and rounD recordings and 8550 scenes, with recording-separated splits and recording-level uncertainty. The input core reaches three-class macro-F1 of 0.816 on controlled and 0.711 on unseen generators; prediction-jitter and response extensions reach 0.827 and 0.830 on controlled data. The response increment is modest, with a paired interval spanning zero. Direct three-class configurations improve unseen tree-model scores; a fixed-weight audit shows that RF differences also reflect class balancing. Magnitude-matched attribution reaches 0.700 on 87 medium/high-severity scenes. Dataset-stratified analyses and shared-scene predictor replication assess stability within the tested design family. Interaction features transfer least reliably, and natural-case assignments neither yield persistent enrichment nor select effective corrections. The study provides a reproducible operating-condition audit and identifies when input signatures, predictor sensitivity, and corrective utility diverge.

title: When Is One Accurate Gradient Query Optimal? Exact Deterministic Bounds under Precision Costs
abstract: We study smooth convex minimization using gradient queries with adversarial absolute errors. A query with absolute error tolerance b > 0 costs 1/b. Algorithms must terminate on every legal instance and satisfy a pathwise budget, but no uniform bound on their number of queries is imposed. In every fixed dimension n ≥ 2, we determine the exact minimax function-gap risk of one deterministic query for every positive error tolerance. At most one query is minimax optimal among all deterministic adaptive strategies for every budget 0 ≤ B ≤ 10; the same values hold for randomized strategies when B ≤ 2. For B ≤ 1, no query is needed. The lower bound uses reflected smooth convex functions that admit a common reply at one expensive query while concealing all cheaper queries through a global gradient bound. An explicit rational certificate shows that two steps of ordinary gradient descent strictly outperform the best deterministic at-most-one-query strategy whenever B ≥ 63/5. The stated conclusions remain valid for continuous stateless oracles without a shared continuity modulus. The one-query optimum also survives a fixed per-query startup cost over a shifted budget interval. Restricted error tolerances and other prices give further consequences. One-query optimality for 10 < B < 63/5 and the exact minimax values for B > 10 remain open.

title: A reconfigurable multi-task diffractive optical processor using phase-multiplexed illumination
abstract: We present a monochrome multi-task diffractive network framework that leverages illumination phase multiplexing to dynamically reconfigure its output transformations. Our design employs unique "phase keys"—distinct 2D illumination phase profiles—to encode specific transformations. The system activates a specific desired transformation simply by adjusting the input illumination phase, enabling programmable processing without physical hardware modifications. We demonstrate that a diffractive network composed of N=2TN_i N_o optimized diffractive features can realize T distinct complex-valued linear transformations – accurately executed for any complex field at the input aperture, where N_i and N_o refer to the input/output pixels, respectively. Proof-of-concept numerical analyses confirmed this phase-multiplexing capability, where T=512 distinct complex-valued transformations were implemented by the same monochrome diffractive network with negligible error. This framework offers a versatile, high-fidelity solution for programmable optical computing, with potential applications in adaptive machine vision and optical information processing.

title: Flexible multi-hop non-destructive teleportation via non-maximally entangled GHZ channels
abstract: Abstract Quantum teleportation is one of the key technologies enabling long-distance quantum communication. However, the decoherence in realistic channels makes it difficult to maintain maximal entanglement. Furthermore, the capability to perform high-dimensional unitary operations poses a significant challenge, as not all the nodes in the quantum network possess this ability. Meanwhile, low transmission rates also hinder the development of quantum networks. We propose a flexible multi-hop non-destructive teleportation via non-maximally entangled GHZ channels, where the network is partitioned into upstream and downstream segments. Direct entanglement channels are established via simultaneous entanglement swapping and multi-level hierarchical swapping. Channel modulation is performed by the selected intermediate parties with high-dimensional operational capabilities and auxiliary particles. In this framework, the sender and the receiver are responsible only for information transmission, while other intermediate nodes perform only basic operations, such as Bell-state and Hadamard (H) measurements. In this scheme, any intermediate node possesses high-dimensional unitary operation capability, making the teleportation process flexible in terms of node deployment and operational responsibility, thereby reducing the requirements for the communication terminals.

title: Cryptography
abstract: This chapter on cryptography focuses on private-key encryption: Alice uses a secret key she shares with Bob to send him an encrypted message over a channel observed by an eavesdropper. Constructions of private-key encryption schemes can be based on pseudorandom generators, which in turn can be based on one-way functions (which are efficiently computable but not efficiently invertible). The chapter also covers constructions of pseudorandom functions, which are more general than pseudorandom generators and have several applications in cryptography and complexity theory.

title: SciCurateBench: Curating Experimental Data from Heterogeneous Scientific Literature with Verbal-Action Agents
abstract: Scientific research increasingly depends on curating experimental data from literature. Scientific data curation requires verifying exact experimental conditions (e.g., specific assays, clinical outcomes, and data availability) across long, heterogeneous files, which is a highly time-consuming process. Existing benchmarks evaluate only broad relevance on short queries, failing to capture this complexity. We introduce SciCurateBench, a benchmark of 200 expert-annotated papers from major life-science journals that challenges systems to verify conjunctive biological experimental criteria from raw, unprocessed scientific literature. We show that plain LLMs and popular reasoning, tool-using, and feedback-based agents all struggle with this task. To study what makes the task tractable, we further propose LangPoli, an integrative system in which a policy agent generates natural language action guidelines that actor agents convert into executable tools. LangPoli showed strong performance on both Paper Classification (83.16% F1 vs. 58.22% for its base LLM) and Structured Information Retrieval, and also improves re-ranking on the public benchmarks of LitSearch, BEIR, and TREC. We further explore curriculum transfer, a method that distills generalizable strategies from solved tasks to accelerate the solving of related problems. We hope this work facilitates research in truly practical scientific AI assistance. The anonymized pre-release can be found from https://anonymous.4open. science/r/scicuratebench-D885/.
