title: Model-agnostic Knowledge Augmented Machine Learning for Weakly Annotated Bioimaging Data
abstract: Machine learning models are increasingly used for automated feature extraction from weakly annotated bioimaging data, such as microscopy and cytomorphology images. Due to the sole dependency of automated feature extraction, existing methods yield inconsistent classification performance across weakly annotated datasets. Here, we propose a model-agnostic knowledge augmentation method that enables ML models to exploit domain knowledge beyond what automated feature extraction can capture. The proposed approach improves classification performance across seven ML architectures. When integrated with masked autoencoder-based self-supervised learning, our method achieves the strongest overall performance, improving precision by 2.9% over the next-best method on three in-house microscopy datasets and by an average of 6.8% across three public cytomorphology benchmarks. We perform nucleus-level classification based on mislocalization of TAR DNA-binding protein 43 (TDP-43) from the nucleus to the cytoplasm, a phenotype linked to Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS), using three independent microscopy datasets of motor neurons derived from human induced pluripotent stem cells. Accurate quantification of this phenotype at scale remains challenging and may contribute to inconsistencies across studies. Application of the best-performing model to these microscopy datasets reveals biological interpretations related to ALS, including dose-dependent effects of the proteasomal stressor, MG132, and the oxidative stressor, sodium arsenite (SA), on TDP-43 mislocalization, variable pathology in motor neurons from sporadic and familial ALS donors, and a lack of protection of the pharmacological compounds, edaravone and niclosamide, against SA-induced TDP-43 mislocalization. Together, our pipeline enables in-vitro cellular image analysis to advance understanding of ALS-associated pathology and potential treatments.

title: Quantum extreme learning for forecasting experimental chaotic electronic circuits
abstract: Quantum reservoir computing and its special case, quantum extreme learning, are powerful tools for predicting classical discrete time-series with quantum devices. Forecasting continuous signals, however, requires careful discretization as oversampling artificially boosts short-term accuracy but fails over realistic intervals, while undersampling captures too few features and yields poor predictions. Here, we experimentally generate four continuous time-series signals from a chaotic electronic circuit for forecasting with quantum extreme learning. Since simplified circuit models do not fully capture real behaviour, it is unclear whether algorithms that predict simulated time-series also work for experimental signals. We address discretization via two approaches: (i) sampling local peaks/troughs; and (ii) uniform sampling at the autocorrelation timescale. The former captures resonant behaviour, while the latter fully captures chaotic features as well as allowing the reconstruction of chaotic attractors. Our algorithm achieves high forecasting accuracy for both simulated and experimental signals, demonstrating its power for continuous signal processing on near-term quantum simulators, and remains robust against moderate decoherence.

title: Quality, Not Just Outcome: A Structural Scoring Framework for Selecting Coding-Agent Trajectories for Supervised Fine-Tuning
abstract: Open coding agents are commonly trained through supervised fine-tuning on interaction trajectories whose final patches pass the benchmark test suite. However, this outcome-level filtering criterion ignores process quality: trajectories that eventually succeed may still contain inefficient interaction patterns such as repetitive file inspection, unstable tool usage, or delayed modification behavior, all of which become part of the imitation target. We propose TQS (Trajectory Quality Score), a structural scoring framework for coding-agent trajectories that operates directly on trajectory structure, requires no LLM judge, and runs in linear time. TQS characterizes trajectory quality through structural signals organized around structured convergence: information focus, intent--action alignment, and policy dynamics. Using 155,144 successful trajectories from a public open-license corpus, we rank trajectories by TQS and fine-tune coding agents on filtered subsets. Models trained on top-ranked trajectories consistently outperform those trained on random or bottom-ranked subsets on SWE-Bench-Verified. Our results suggest that process-level trajectory quality is an important factor in coding-agent supervision and that structural trajectory filtering provides an effective and scalable alternative to LLM-based data selection.

title: TopoLIA: Topology-Inspired Latent Interaction Attention for Drug Discovery
abstract: The growing sophistication of drug discovery calls for new advances in artificial intelligence (AI). Transformers have underpinned recent breakthroughs in AI, yet their conventional source-target attention mechanism can become a bottleneck for modeling complex interactions. Here, we introduce TopoLIA, a topology-inspired latent interaction attention mechanism that learns not only how much information should be exchanged between interaction partners, but also how that information should be transformed. Source-target-dependent attention is mediated through a compact latent interaction space, providing a structured representation of complex interactions. We further incorporate topological spectral representations to capture multiscale data geometry and extract algebraic relationships. TopoLIA thus incorporates topological principles into both data representation and neural network architecture. We demonstrate TopoLIA on protein-ligand binding, where persistent spectra encode multiscale topological and geometric patterns in 3D protein-ligand complexes, while latent interaction attention (LIA) enables structured, source-target-dependent information exchange. We pretrain TopoLIA by reconstructing masked multiscale spectral tokens from unlabeled molecular structures, yielding transferable structural representations without task-specific annotations. Across multiple scoring and docking benchmarks, TopoLIA achieves state-of-the-art performance and consistently outperforms its standard-attention counterpart. Rank analyses show that compact latent dimensions yield the best performance, supporting compact interaction spaces as an effective inductive bias for biomolecular learning. More broadly, LIA provides a general framework for structured, source-target-dependent information exchange that is applicable to diverse scientific and AI problems involving complex heterogeneous interactions.

title: AI-Mediation in Retail Markets: Revenue Effects and Assortment Optimization
abstract: AI shopping assistants increasingly influence which products consumers consider. We study retail assortment planning under AI mediation, where a retailer chooses a catalog, an AI intermediary forms a customer-facing shortlist, and the customer chooses from that shortlist according to a multinomial logit model. We consider both deterministic mediation, in which the AI follows a fixed segment-specific ranking, and stochastic mediation based on the Plackett-Luce model. Empirically, we construct a dataset of product rankings from leading AI models, estimate Plackett-Luce ranking models, and evaluate their predictive performance on held-out assortments. Combining these estimates with synthetic customer preferences, we find that accounting for AI mediation can materially change optimal assortments and revenue. Across the tested capacity configurations, ignoring mediation yields mean revenue losses between 2.52% and 11.37% relative to the PL optimum. A much simpler deterministic plug-in, based only on the ordering of fitted AI utilities, performs substantially better, with mean losses of at most 0.53%. Motivated by this performance, we study assortment optimization under deterministic mediation. We characterize its computational complexity and show that, for any fixed number of customer segments, the problem admits a fully polynomial-time approximation scheme.

title: Compatible-Marginal Spin Alignment for Three Qubits
abstract: The strong spin-alignment conjecture fails for three qubits when the subset states are chosen independently. We prove that it holds when they are marginals of one global state: for every three-qubit state, every positive semidefinite qubit operator Q, and every nonnegative set of subset weights, the aligned output majorizes the corresponding marginal mixture. The proof classifies the extreme rays of cones on which a fixed set of aligned eigenvalues is largest. This reduces arbitrary weights to two-term sums and the complete one- and two-body layers. For arbitrary numbers of subsystems, we also characterize when one unital quantum channel simultaneously realizes all marginal replacements. This criterion proves alignment for fully PPT states. A separate argument proves alignment for locally rotated stabilizer states in every prime local dimension, at maximally mixed background. These results determine the minimum output Rényi entropies of the associated three-qubit replacement channels. Under either of the two input restrictions above, they also determine the many-use classical capacity and the exact strong-converse exponent for correlated replacement channels of arbitrary size.

Under either of the two input restrictions above, they also determine the many-use classical capacity and the exact strong-converse exponent for correlated replacement channels of arbitrary size.

title: Classifying Phase-Only DSP Filters as QFT-Diagonal Quantum Operators
abstract: This paper presents a theoretical classification framework for phase-only digital signal processing filters interpreted as Quantum Fourier Transform diagonal quantum operators. It builds on an earlier DSP-to-QFT filtering framework and focuses on identifying which DSP-inspired filter responses can be directly implemented as valid quantum operations.The main result is that only phase-only sampled filter responses are directly compatible with unitary quantum gates. This means that ordinary magnitude-changing filters, such as classical low-pass or high-pass filters, cannot be implemented directly as quantum gates without additional methods such as ancilla systems, block encoding, post-selection, or unitary dilation.The paper connects the framework to circulant operator theory, showing that direct QFT-diagonal quantum filters correspond to circulant unitary operators. This gives the framework a clearer mathematical foundation and separates valid unitary quantum filters from non-unitary classical filtering operations.Several structured examples are analysed, including delay filters, linear phase filters, polynomial phase filters, and chirp-like filters. Delay filters are shown to produce cyclic shifts in the computational basis, making them useful as simple building blocks for modular shifts and quantum-walk-style operations. The paper also discusses how structured phase filters can have compact descriptions, while arbitrary phase filters may require exponentially many parameters.The central design principle is that direct QFT-diagonal quantum filters must be phase-only, while practical or efficient implementations require compact phase structure. The paper does not claim a new quantum speedup, but instead provides a DSP-inspired classification and design perspective for valid unitary QFT-diagonal quantum filters.

title: Measuring the Inference Energy Efficiency of Open-Weight LLMs across Benchmarks, Reasoning Modes, and Hardware
abstract: Benchmark scores tell us what an LLM can do, but not how much energy is required to deliver that capability. We directly measure this trade-off for 86 open-weight model checkpoints, evaluated on seven benchmarks and six hardware platforms ranging from a consumer GPU to an eight-GPU server. We find large differences in energy efficiency even among models with similar capability. Most configurations lie away from the score--energy Pareto frontier: they use a median of 2.6--4.8$\times$ more energy than another configuration that scores at least as well, with differences reaching 27$\times$. Reasoning can improve capability, but enabling thinking increases energy by about 3.7$\times$ on average, and the benefit depends strongly on the model family and output budget. Generated-token count is also an imperfect proxy for energy, misordering 18--24\% of model pairs. In contrast, FP8 reduces energy by roughly a quarter with little change in score, while changing hardware largely rescales energy without changing the relative ranking of models. These results show that capability alone gives an incomplete picture of efficiency. We argue that benchmark scores should be reported together with measured energy consumption under a specified serving regime and output budget.

title: Information-Weighted Distributed Kalman Filter for Multi-Target Tracking over Switching Sensor Networks
abstract: Target tracking over wide areas using a network of sensor agents is a challenging problem when agents have limited sensing coverage and communication topologies vary over time. Existing distributed filtering approaches commonly assume that each agent, or at least one of its neighbors, can directly observe the target, and further rely on fixed network topologies, global network parameters, or multiple consensus rounds per time step. These requirements limit their applicability in wide-area network deployments. In this paper, we propose an Information-Weighted Distributed Kalman Filter (IWDKF) that relaxes these assumptions through a weighted-consensus mechanism applicable to arbitrary switching topologies satisfying joint connectivity. The proposed approach requires no prior knowledge of global network properties and limits communication overhead to a single consensus exchange per time step, while enabling information fusion even when some agents lack direct target measurements. The weighted-consensus covariance matrix is shown to remain positive definite, and the resulting consensus update is proven to maintain estimate consistency. It is also established that the proposed weighting strategy preserves the asymptotic agreement property of the underlying consensus protocol under joint connectivity. Numerical simulations of a multi-target tracking scenario involving a network of sensor agents demonstrate the improved estimation accuracy of the proposed IWDKF under both fixed and switching network topologies. The performance of the proposed filter is close to that of the centralized Kalman filter, and is compared with three existing distributed filters.

title: Benchmarking Answer-Grounding Consistency in Remote Sensing Visual Question Answering
abstract: In grounded remote sensing visual question answering, a model produces a textual answer and identifies relevant objects in the image as grounding evidence. Existing evaluations measure answer correctness and localization quality, but do not directly assess answer-grounding consistency. We propose the Answer-Evidence Support Protocol (AESP) to assess this consistency through evidence support: whether the grounding evidence supports the model's own answer. AESP applies task-specific rules to existence, counting, and comparison questions. We further construct the Grounded Remote Sensing Visual Question Answering (G-RSVQA) benchmark, containing 15,027 samples with questions, reference answers, and all related object-level annotations. Experiments on seven grounded vision--language models reveal failures of evidence support across all three question types. Up to 50.82% of correct answers in the evidence evaluation subset are not supported by the provided grounding evidence.

title: BLOKS: Scaling Kernel Solvers with Sketched Block Preconditioning
abstract: Kernel Ridge Regression (KRR) is a theoretically sound algorithm for nonparametric learning, which is also often used to investigate properties of deep learning. However, the exact KRR formulation incurs time and memory costs preventing applicability to large datasets, motivating the development of approximate solvers. These algorithms rely on (i) iterative methods, to avoid the computational burden of direct solutions; (ii) sketching or batching, to reduce the problem size; and (iii) preconditioning, to accelerate convergence. While crucial for fast convergence, preconditioning incurs memory costs that can be managed by lowering the number of free parameters of the model, potentially at the expense of expressivity and hence accuracy. To address this challenge, we propose BLOKS, a Conjugate Gradient-based solver for Nyström-sketched KRR built around a novel preconditioner that combines a block Jacobi approximation with sketching. The BLOKS preconditioner has memory cost independent of both the dataset size and the number of parameters, allowing scaling to large models. We provide a memory-efficient, GPU-accelerated implementation and show that BLOKS achieves excellent accuracy while retaining favorable time/memory complexity. Indeed, on standard large-scale datasets used to benchmark kernel solvers, BLOKS achieves comparable or better performances than state-of-the-art methods.

title: Les Misérables Dialogue: A film-based network representation of social communication
abstract: In this work, we revisit the classic Les Misérables benchmark network from the perspective of social communication. Using the 1998 film adaptation of the novel, we construct the publicly available Les Misérables Dialogue temporal text network, which explicitly distinguishes speakers, addressees, and other recipients of each utterance, along with its content and timing. Using the ten social dimensions model, we also derive multilayer network representations of the network, in which layers correspond to distinct relational dimensions. Beyond the network dataset, this work offers a general methodology for building similarly rich communication datasets from similar narrative sources.

title: DeFiRank: Federated Pairwise Ranking for Governance in Decentralized Financial Networks
abstract: Existing governance approaches in decentralized financial networks rely on manual review processes conducted by human committees, which introduces subjective bias, creates a scalability bottleneck under high network volume, and fails to capture complex behavioural patterns and evolving network dynamics. To address these limitations, we propose \name, a federated learning-based pairwise ranking framework in which multiple institutions collaboratively train a ranking model without sharing their private transaction data. This collaborative learning enables the model to capture network-wide behavioural patterns that signify strong network participation and directly contribute to the network effect, including diversity of counterparties, usage of multiple applications, and frequency of transactions. The proposed system ranks providers based on the authenticity of their actions, promoting genuine contributors and demoting those exhibiting suspicious behaviour. We evaluate \name\ on a real-world blockchain transaction dataset. Results demonstrate that the federated approach achieves ranking performance modestly below the centralized baseline (NDCG@15: $\approx$0.87 vs.\ $\approx$0.92) while preserving data privacy and matching its ranking stability (Kendall $τ$: $\approx$0.70 for both regimes), producing reliable governance decisions, including provider promotion and demotion (648 and 39 unique providers, respectively), without requiring centralized access to sensitive transaction data.

title: The Managerial Blind Spot Effect Explainable Machine Learning for Strategic Decision-Making
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is used in strategic decision-making; however, it is not clear whether the use of explainable machine learning leads to more managerial judgment when prediction accuracy is high. This study analyzes the proposed ‘Managerial Blind Spot Effect’ by combining predictive modelling with behavioural analysis applied to the IBM Telco Customer Churn dataset and the AI Decision Dependence and Cognitive Caution dataset. Several models, including Explanatory Boosting Machine (EBM), XGBoost, Random Forest and Neural Network, were tested, and the explanation produced by the native model EBM was enhanced by SHAP-based explanation. The behavioural results revealed that both Trust in AI and Cognitive Caution significantly contributed to an increase in AI Dependence. EBM delivered the best predictive performance with intrinsic transparency. The results highlight the importance of using explainable AI prediction models in conjunction with managerial judgment in dashboards.

title: الذكاء الاصطناعي وهندسة الأداء: من الابتكار التوليدي إلى القيمة المؤسسية المستدامة
abstract: يقدم كتاب "الذكاء الاصطناعي وهندسة الأداء: من الابتكار التوليدي إلى القيمة المؤسسية المستدامة" (من إعداد د. عابدة الحناوي) دليلاً شاملاً يجمع بين الأبعاد التقنية، الإدارية، الأخلاقية، والاستشرافية للذكاء الاصطناعي وكيفية تحويله إلى قيمة مؤسسية مستدامة. ينقسم الكتاب إلى ثلاثة أجزاء رئيسية تندرج تحتها 10 فصول بالإضافة إلى الملحقات: الجزء الأول: الأسس والتطبيقات التقنية (الفصول 1 - 3) الفصل الأول (نشأة الذكاء الاصطناعي وتطوره): يستعرض تاريخ الذكاء الاصطناعي بدءاً من الجذور الفلسفية واختبار تورينج (1950) ومؤتمر دارتماوث (1956)، مروراً بفترات "الشتاء" ووصولاً إلى "ربيع التعلم العميق" (2012) وظهور المعماريات الحديثة وChatGPT. الفصل الثاني (الأسس التقنية للذكاء الاصطناعي): يشرح الوحدات الأساسية للشبكات العصبية، خوارزمية الانتشار الخلفي، أنواع التعلم الثلاثة (الموجه، غير الموجه، والمعزز)، ومعمارية الترانسفورمر ($Attention\ is\ All\ You\ Need$) وآليات التدريب والضبط الدقيق. الفصل الثالث (النماذج اللغوية الكبيرة وتطبيقاتها): يغطي مهارات وقوالب هندسة الأوامر، معمارية تعزيز الاسترجاع (RAG) لربط النماذج بقواعد المعرفة، بنية الوكلاء الأذكياء (AI Agents)، مقارنة النماذج الكبرى ($GPT-4$, $Claude\ 3$, $Gemini$, $Llama\ 3$)، وتقنيات الضبط الدقيق الخفيف مثل LoRA. الجزء الثاني: البعد الإداري والأخلاقي (الفصول 4 - 5) الفصل الرابع (الذكاء الاصطناعي في الأعمال والاستراتيجية): يقدم أدوات استراتيجية مثل "مصفوفة التطبيقات" لتحديد الأولويات بحسب الأثر وسهولة التطبيق، "منحنى النضج المؤسسي" (من الوعي إلى الريادة)، نماذج الأعمال الجديدة، كيفية حساب العائد على الاستثمار (ROI)، وبناء الفرق وتحديد المواهب. الفصل الخامس (آداب وأخلاقيات الذكاء الاصطناعي): يناقش إطار الحوكمة الأخلاقية المتكامل (الشفافية، العدالة، الخصوصية، المساءلة، الأمان، الاستدامة، والإنسانية)، معالجة التحيز الخوارزمي، قوانين الخصوصية العالمية والأوروبية ($EU\ AI\ Act$)، وفجوة المسؤولية القانونية. الجزء الثالث: رؤى مستقبلية واستشرافية (الفصول 6 - 10) الفصل السادس (الحوكمة اللامركزية): يتناول مخاطر احتكار القوة التقنية في شركات محدودة، ويكشف عن بدائل الذكاء الاصطناعي اللامركزي المستند إلى الحوسبة الموزعة والديمقراطية الحسابية والمنظمات المستقلة (DAOs). الفصل السابع (اقتصاد المعرفة وثورة ما بعد الرأسمالية): يشرح كيف أصبحت الأفكار والمعرفة هي رأس المال الأساسي المكرس للوفرة، وتأثير الذكاء الاصطناعي كمضاعف للمعرفة، ومفهوم "رموز المعرفة" والدخل الأساسي المعرفي. الفصل الثامن (الإصلاح الكوكبي بالذكاء الاصطناعي): يستعرض منظومة سداسية لتطبيقات الذكاء الاصطناعي في معالجة الأزمات البيئية والمناخية (الطاقة المتجددة، الزراعة الذكية، تنقية المحيطات، إعادة التشجير، التقاط الكربون، والتنبؤ المناخي). الفصل التاسع (تعايش الإنسان والآلة): يتتبع طيف العلاقة مع الآلة من مجرد "أداة" إلى "امتداد" ذي هوية هجينة، والشراكة العاطفية والتحديات الفلسفية لما بعد الإنسانية والتربية الإنسانية. الفصل العاشر (التعلم العصبي وآفاق الذكاء العام): يستشرف المستقبل القريب والبعيد لتطور أنظمة التعلم، واجهات الدماغ والحاسوب (BCI) والتعلم العصبي المباشر، ومسارات الوصول للذكاء الاصطناعي العام (AGI) والتحديات الأخلاقية المرتبطة به. الملحقات والأدوات البصرية خريطة ذهنية شاملة: تجمع محاور رحلة احتراف الذكاء الاصطناعي في لوحة واحدة. فهرس مصطلحات: يحتوي على أكثر من 30 مصطلحاً تقنياً مشروحاً باللغتين العربية والإنجليزية.

3) الفصل الأول (نشأة الذكاء الاصطناعي وتطوره): يستعرض تاريخ الذكاء الاصطناعي بدءاً من الجذور الفلسفية واختبار تورينج (1950) ومؤتمر دارتماوث (1956)، مروراً بفترات "الشتاء" ووصولاً إلى "ربيع التعلم العميق" (2012) وظهور المعماريات الحديثة وChatGPT. الفصل الثاني (الأسس التقنية للذكاء الاصطناعي): يشرح الوحدات الأساسية للشبكات العصبية، خوارزمية الانتشار الخلفي، أنواع التعلم الثلاثة (الموجه، غير الموجه، والمعزز)، ومعمارية الترانسفورمر ($Attention\ is\ All\ You\ Need$) وآليات التدريب والضبط الدقيق. الفصل الثالث (النماذج اللغوية الكبيرة وتطبيقاتها): يغطي مهارات وقوالب هندسة الأوامر، معمارية تعزيز الاسترجاع (RAG) لربط النماذج بقواعد المعرفة، بنية الوكلاء الأذكياء (AI Agents)، مقارنة النماذج الكبرى ($GPT-4$, $Claude\ 3$, $Gemini$, $Llama\ 3$)، وتقنيات الضبط الدقيق الخفيف مثل LoRA. الجزء الثاني: البعد الإداري والأخلاقي (الفصول 4 - 5) الفصل الرابع (الذكاء الاصطناعي في الأعمال والاستراتيجية): يقدم أدوات استراتيجية مثل "مصفوفة التطبيقات" لتحديد الأولويات بحسب الأثر وسهولة التطبيق، "منحنى النضج المؤسسي" (من الوعي إلى الريادة)، نماذج الأعمال الجديدة، كيفية حساب العائد على الاستثمار (ROI)، وبناء الفرق وتحديد المواهب. الفصل الخامس (آداب وأخلاقيات الذكاء الاصطناعي): يناقش إطار الحوكمة الأخلاقية المتكامل (الشفافية، العدالة، الخصوصية، المساءلة، الأمان، الاستدامة، والإنسانية)، معالجة التحيز الخوارزمي، قوانين الخصوصية العالمية والأوروبية ($EU\ AI\ Act$)، وفجوة المسؤولية القانونية. الجزء الثالث: رؤى مستقبلية واستشرافية (الفصول 6 - 10) الفصل السادس (الحوكمة اللامركزية): يتناول مخاطر احتكار القوة التقنية في شركات محدودة، ويكشف عن بدائل الذكاء الاصطناعي اللامركزي المستند إلى الحوسبة الموزعة والديمقراطية الحسابية والمنظمات المستقلة (DAOs). الفصل السابع (اقتصاد المعرفة وثورة ما بعد الرأسمالية): يشرح كيف أصبحت الأفكار والمعرفة هي رأس المال الأساسي المكرس للوفرة، وتأثير الذكاء الاصطناعي كمضاعف للمعرفة، ومفهوم "رموز المعرفة" والدخل الأساسي المعرفي. الفصل الثامن (الإصلاح الكوكبي بالذكاء الاصطناعي): يستعرض منظومة سداسية لتطبيقات الذكاء الاصطناعي في معالجة الأزمات البيئية والمناخية (الطاقة المتجددة، الزراعة الذكية، تنقية المحيطات، إعادة التشجير، التقاط الكربون، والتنبؤ المناخي). الفصل التاسع (تعايش الإنسان والآلة): يتتبع طيف العلاقة مع الآلة من مجرد "أداة" إلى "امتداد" ذي هوية هجينة، والشراكة العاطفية والتحديات الفلسفية لما بعد الإنسانية والتربية الإنسانية. الفصل العاشر (التعلم العصبي وآفاق الذكاء العام): يستشرف المستقبل القريب والبعيد لتطور أنظمة التعلم، واجهات الدماغ والحاسوب (BCI) والتعلم العصبي المباشر، ومسارات الوصول للذكاء الاصطناعي العام (AGI) والتحديات الأخلاقية المرتبطة به. الملحقات والأدوات البصرية خريطة ذهنية شاملة: تجمع محاور رحلة احتراف الذكاء الاصطناعي في لوحة واحدة. فهرس مصطلحات: يحتوي على أكثر من 30 مصطلحاً تقنياً مشروحاً باللغتين العربية والإنجليزية.

title: bcfOWL: BIM Collaboration Format Ontology
abstract: bcfOWL represents the BIM Collaboration Format (BCF) in RDF. It does not translate the BCF schema one to one. It composes BCF from established vocabularies (SOSA, SPOT, PROV-O, DCAT, SKOS, Dublin Core) and keeps only the coordination concepts that no other vocabulary covers, such as Topic, Comment, Viewpoint, and the visual state. Version 1.0.0 moves the ontology to the persistent namespace https://w3id.org/bcfOWL#.

title: An Explainable Disease-Aware Intelligent Histopathological Representation Learning Framework for Generalizable Breast Cancer Classification
abstract: Background: Deep learning approaches, especially convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and Vision Transformers (ViTs), have made substantial progress in breast cancer classification from histopathological images. Yet, previous CNN–ViT-based architectures frequently demonstrate insufficient generalization when evaluated on independent external datasets despite obtaining high performance on internal benchmarks. The key reason is that these architectures learn statistical dependencies instead of precisely identifying disease-specific morphological evidence. During optimization, models may unintentionally depend on non-diagnostic patterns, such as staining variations, scanner characteristics, acquisition settings, and dataset-specific textures, thereby potentially becoming aligned with class labels in the training data but not reflecting intrinsic pathological patterns. This phenomenon leads to inconsistent predictions under domain shifts. Methods: To overcome this limitation, this study proposes a disease-aware intelligent histopathological representation learning framework for generalizable breast cancer classification. The proposed framework leverages CNN and ViT encoders to capture complementary local cellular morphology and global tissue-level contextual information. A disease-aware representation learning mechanism is introduced to distinguish clinically relevant disease-specific features from non-diagnostic fluctuations, allowing the model to concentrate on transferable pathological features. Additionally, an intelligent adaptive decision module is designed to optimize the use of clinically relevant disease evidence for benign and malignant classification instead of relying on the conventional classification head. Results: The proposed framework is evaluated on BreakHis as the internal benchmark (98.10% accuracy) and various independent histopathology datasets for external validation. Conclusions: Comprehensive experiments, robustness analysis, and explainability analyses highlight the effectiveness of the proposed approach in learning generalizable disease-related representations and improving the consistency of cross-dataset breast cancer classification.

title: Linking geothermal reservoir and lithium distribution: A handheld spectroscopy approach on deep wells in the Upper Rhine Graben
abstract: The Upper Rhine Graben (URG) hosts a deep geothermal system characterized by fluid circulation within fractured reservoirs at the sedimentary-basement interface. This study investigates cuttings from two deep geothermal wells in the Strasbourg area to assess how reservoir heterogeneity and hydrothermal circulation influence alteration and lithium distribution. Cuttings collected below 3.8 km true vertical depth cover lithologies from the Buntsandstein sandstones to the Carboniferous granitic basement. Reservoir characterization was performed using handheld SWIR (Short-Wave Infrared) and LIBS (Laser-Induced Breakdown Spectroscopy) spectrometers as rapid screening tools, complemented by laboratory analyses, to characterise alteration and lithium zonation at the well scale. The results reveal strong heterogeneity in fracture-related alteration patterns and lithium-enriched fluid circulations in the reservoir. Lithium-enriched geothermal brines, with concentrations up to ∼200 ppm, are interpreted to circulate preferentially along fault and fracture networks, promoting sustained fluid–rock interactions. Variations in lithium content correlate with distinct alteration facies, highlighting the role of clay minerals and carbonates during hydrothermal circulation. These findings support a conceptual geothermal model in which structurally controlled fluid flow governs lithium-bearing brine circulation in the URG, with implications for geothermal projects targeting the co-extraction of heat and lithium.

title: Quantum Signal Processing Phase Factorization via Logarithmic Derivatives
abstract: Quantum signal processing (QSP) requires the efficient computation of phase factors associated with a polynomial transformation. One existing stable factorization method avoids direct root finding but relies on Prony's method to recover a polynomial from weighted power sums of its roots (arXiv:2202.02671). We present a modification of this approach that eliminates Prony's method by using the logarithmic derivative of an associated polynomial. Because the logarithmic derivative has the same residue at every root after accounting for multiplicity, its Fourier coefficients directly yield the unweighted power sums of the roots inside the unit disk. The Newton--Girard identities then recover the coefficients of the corresponding polynomial without computing its roots. The resulting algorithm has $O(d\log^2 d)$ computational complexity and simplifies the factorization procedure of the original method. In numerical experiments on Hamiltonian simulation, eigenstate filtering, matrix inversion, and the Fermi--Dirac operator, our implementation computes phase factors in seconds with maximum errors on the order of $10^{-12}$.

title: Real Fiducial Vectors Only Exist in Dimensions $d\equiv 3 \pmod{4}$
abstract: We investigate restrictions on the dimensions and coordinate fields of real Weyl-Heisenberg fiducial vectors. Our main result is that such vectors can exist only in dimensions $d\equiv 3\pmod{4}$. This result is motivated by evidence showing that real Weyl-Heisenberg fiducial vectors can exist only in dimensions $d = 4m^2 + 3, m \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$. We further restrict the possible dimensions when the coordinate field is a totally real number field, an even or odd degree extension of $\mathbb{Q}$, a real quadratic field, or a maximal real subfield of a cyclotomic field. Lastly, we establish non-existence over odd-degree number fields under either positivity of all non-trivial cyclic-shift overlaps or a conjectural containment of a distinguished quadratic field in the SIC field.

title: VIGOR: Verifiable Industrial Geometry Optimization and Repair in Scene Programs
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly generate structured layouts and executable scene programs from natural-language instructions. However, executability does not imply engineering feasibility: an industrial scene program may execute successfully while its final state still violates coupled boundary, collision, clearance, aisle, or structural constraints. We identify this mismatch as the executability-engineering-feasibility gap, where locally plausible placements can remain globally infeasible because corrections to one device may introduce violations elsewhere. To make this gap measurable in a controlled setting, we construct an execution-grounded industrial scene-program dataset with 1,749 constructible scenarios, complete executable programs, and 94 final-state geometric checks per scenario. We further propose VIGOR, which combines supervised scene-program generation with execution-grounded verification and staged geometric refinement. Supervised fine-tuning establishes complete program generation, local projection resolves independently correctable violations, and joint conflict-graph repair coordinates residual multi-object conflicts while preserving structural relations. Experiments show that VIGOR achieves 96.86% Complete Feasibility and an Overall score of 91.20, outperforming the strongest evaluated baseline by 10.42 points in Overall. These results show that, under controlled industrial layout conditions, reliable scene-program generation requires not only executable programs, but also explicit verification and coordinated resolution of coupled engineering constraints.

title: Design of an AI-IoT-ML Framework for Intelligent Physics Education and Evidence-Based Educational Administration in Smart Learning Environments
abstract: The increasing integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI), Internet of Things (IoT), and Machine Learning (ML) is creating new opportunities for intelligent and data-informed educational environments. However, applications of these technologies in physics education are often fragmented across instructional support, assessment, learning analytics, laboratory activities and institutional management, limiting their integration into a unified educational decision-support system. This study therefore designed an AI-IoT-ML framework for intelligent physics education and evidence-based educational administration in smart learning environments. The study adopted a Design Science Research (DSR) approach involving problem identification, objective definition, framework design and development, demonstration, conceptual evaluation, and communication. The proposed framework integrates a smart physics environment, IoT-based data acquisition, data processing and storage, ML analytics and prediction, AI decision support, and physics education and educational administration into a layered architecture with a continuous feedback mechanism. The framework provides potential applications in physics teaching and learning, student support, laboratory monitoring, equipment utilisation, resource management, scheduling, maintenance planning and evidence-based administrative decision-making. A key feature of the framework is its human-centred orientation, in which AI and ML provide analytical insights and recommendations while educators and administrators retain responsibility for professional judgement and final decisions. The study contributes a conceptual and architectural artefact that addresses the fragmentation between smart learning technologies, physics education and educational administration. The framework provides a foundation for subsequent prototype development, simulation and empirical evaluation of intelligent physics learning environments.

title: NUTQ KORPUSINI ANNOTATSIYALASHNING LINGVISTIK ASOSLARI: SAMARQAND VILOYATI SHEVASI MISOLIDA
abstract: Mazkur maqolada o‘zbek tili shevalariga, xususan, Samarqand shevasiga asoslangan nutq texnologiyalari (STT va TTS) uchun mo‘ljallangan audio korpuslarni annotatsiyalashning lingvistik asoslari tahlil qilinadi. Maqolada annotatsiyalash jarayonining ketma-ket bosqichlari – audio sifatini nazorat qilish va segmentatsiya, so‘zma-so‘z transkripsiya tamoyili, orfografik me’yorlash, dialektal xususiyatlarni normallashtirmaslik tamoyili, kod almashinish hodisasining belgilanishi – nazariy jihatdan asoslanadi va amaliy misollar bilan yoritiladi. title: Spatial search by pseudo-Hermitian continuous-time quantum walks
abstract: Abstract We apply pseudo-Hermitian continuous-time quantum walks to the spatial search problem, derive exact analytical solutions for the resulting dynamics, and determine the first hitting time at which the target probability is maximal. In an idealized setting with a fixed coupling strength g, we show that the formal first-maximum time t = π / g is independent of the database size N . However, we emphasize that this does not imply a general complexity improvement: making t = π / g arbitrarily small requires a corresponding increase in the Hamiltonian matrix elements (energy scale), a fundamental resource trade-off. A fair assessment must also account for the measurement and postselection overhead required to extract the target probability and for the cost of implementing the evolution. Our results provide an analytically tractable non-Hermitian model that supports state preparation and parameter-controlled quantum dynamics.

title: A Semantic Framework for the Assessment and Management of Historic Timber Structures: Linking CIDOC CRM-Based Ontological Modelling and HBIM
abstract: The conservation of historic timber structures requires the continuous collection and updating of heterogeneous information related to both historical development and structural safety. Data coming from repeated maintenance surveys and on-site assessments are often fragmented, difficult to compare, and poorly structured for long-term use. This study proposes a semantic framework for the assessment and management of historic timber structures, whose applicability is demonstrated through its application to the timber roof structure of the San Marco Museum in Florence. The methodology defines the knowledge domain specific to historic timber structure assessment and formalises it through an ontological model aligned with the CIDOC Conceptual Reference Model (CRM) and its extensions CRMba and CRMsci. The ontology is implemented in Web Ontology Language (OWL) using the Protégé editor, populated with individual instances, and queried through SPARQL, while an HBIM environment provides the spatial and operational context for data organisation and visualisation. The two systems are linked through a shared identifier system. The results demonstrate that the proposed framework enables the structured integration and querying of heterogeneous diagnostic data, supporting their long-term management while preserving provenance, temporal context, and methodological information.

title: Securing Enterprise DevOps: Zero Trust Architecture in Cloud-Native and Microservices Environments
abstract: Abstract—Modern enterprise software engineering has undergone an architectural paradigm shift toward cloud-native architectures, containerized microservices, and high-velocity continuous integration and continuous deployment (CI/CD) pipelines. Concurrently, legacy perimeter-based security models ('castle-and-moat') have proven entirely inadequate in distributed, multi-tenant cloud ecosystems where internal network boundaries are non-existent and lateral movement vectors abound. The integration of Zero Trust Architecture (ZTA)—grounded in the foundational tenet of 'never trust, always verify'—into enterprise DevOps pipelines establishes an end-to-end security framework spanning code authoring, artifact signing, workload attestation, and runtime execution. However, embedding continuous, multi-dimensional verification into automated deployment pipelines introduces acute tensions between developer velocity, cryptographic verification latency, operational overhead, and distributed policy consistency. This paper provides an exshaustive, mathematically grounded technical investigation and architectural synthesis of Zero Trust DevOps (DevSecOps) across cloud-native environments. We formalize workload identity mechanics utilizing the SPIFFE/SPIRE cryptographic framework, model service-mesh-based mutual Transport Layer Security (mTLS) enforcement with sidecar and ambient proxies, and formalize Policy-as-Code (PaC) invariants under Open Policy Agent (OPA) gatekeepers. Furthermore, we implement an empirical enterprise testbed comprising 120 containerized microservices deployed across a production-grade Kubernetes cluster, subjected to automated adversarial red-team injection vectors (including supply-chain dependency poisoning, stolen credential replay, and kernel escape exploits). Our empirical findings demonstrate that an optimized Zero Trust posture reduces lateral attack propagation by 96.4% and halts software supply-chain compromises at the CI boundary with an operational latency penalty of only 4.8% on end-to-end pipeline execution. Finally, we formulate open challenges in post-quantum cryptographic workload attestation, continuous behavioral policy synthesis, and automated zero-knowledge secretless pipelines. Index Terms—Zero Trust Architecture (ZTA), Cloud-Native Systems, Microservices, DevSecOps, SPIFFE/SPIRE, Service Mesh, Policy-as-Code, Open Policy Agent (OPA), Supply Chain Security, eBPF Runtime Security.

title: Improved two-way capacity upper bounds for amplitude-damping channels
abstract: Abstract: We derive an improved upper bound on the two-way-assisted capacities of the qubit amplitude-damping channel with decay probability $\gamma$, given by $\log_2[1+(1-\gamma)\gamma^{\gamma/(1-\gamma)}]$. It applies to quantum communication, entanglement distribution, private communication, and secret-key agreement, and strictly improves the PLOB relative-entropy bound, the analytic max-relative-entropy bound, and the optimized balanced squashed-entanglement bound. At high damping, a known triple-rail protocol attains more than $99.54\%$ of its leading coefficient. Our method extends sector teleportation simulation to qubits: phase rotations and permutations give exact simulations within fixed-excitation subspaces while preserving the two-level input structure. We determine the exact, additive relative entropy of entanglement of the amplitude-damping resources and the exact regularized entanglement gain at fixed input population. We then derive explicit bounds for generalized amplitude damping, which includes thermal excitation. Combining the amplitude-damping gain with unital and entanglement-breaking channels gives a closed expression that recovers the zero-temperature result and vanishes throughout the entanglement-breaking region. It improves established benchmarks over broad parameter ranges, while the exact entanglement of the generalized resources remains open. Both results admit refinements under an average-excitation constraint. The bounds provide quantitative limits for adaptive communication through relaxing qubits and show how a sector simulation can remain useful beyond channels whose resource entanglement is known exactly.

title: Adaptive Knowledge Consolidation for Sequential Learning in Deep Neural Networks
abstract: Catastrophic forgetting is a major challenge in sequential deep learning, where learning new tasks can degrade previously acquired knowledge, particularly in evolving healthcare applications. Existing approaches mainly rely on replay, regularization, or architectural strategies, while the integration of adaptive, biologically inspired sleep mechanisms in conventional deep networks remains limited. To address this gap, this paper proposes a conceptual Adaptive Knowledge Consolidation (AKC) framework integrating wake-phase learning, NREM-inspired replay, REM-inspired knowledge integration, synaptic homeostasis, and adaptive sleep scheduling. The framework is designed for sequential image classification, with planned validation using Alzheimer?s disease-related brain MRI data. Evaluation will consider accuracy, forgetting measure, backward and forward transfer, sensitivity, specificity, F1-score, and AUROC. As implementation is ongoing, no numerical results are claimed. The study establishes the framework, mathematical formulation, and experimental protocol for future empirical validation.

title: Another look at universal one-to-one codes
abstract: For universal prefix codes, redundancy separates into a Θ(logn) predictor component and an O(1) coding component. Kosut and Sankar showed that dropping the prefix constraint cuts universal redundancy by logn—far more than the prefix code costs. We locate the origin of this gain by deterministic counting in Shtarkov’s single-transmission setting. The optimal universal one-to-one code ranks sequences by increasing empirical entropy, with redundancy exactly R1:1n = maxh[⌊log2 Bn(h)⌋−nh], with Bn(h) the number of sequences whose empirical entropy does not exceed h. Both code classes face the same object: the mass the maximized likelihood places on unit shells of empirical entropy. Prefix codes, bound by one Kraft budget, pay the logarithm of the total mass; one-to-one codes pay only that of the heaviest shell. For memoryless sources the mass spans Θ(n) shells, and the removed logn is the cost of aggregating the predictor’s regret across them—equivalently, of the level pointer that a self-delimiting codeword must carry and a transport-delimited ranking gets for free. The same formula yields finite-n bounds for all alphabet sizes and R1:1n = 1 bit for binary sources at all n.

title: Opening the Black Box of Classifier-Free Guidance via Information Bottleneck
abstract: Classifier-free guidance (CFG) is a standard technique for improving conditional generation in diffusion models, yet its activation schedule is usually selected heuristically. In practice, most existing CFG-based methods rely on a pre-defined activation policy throughout inference, while recent dynamic variants often depend on hand-designed schedules without a principled theoretical explanation of when conditional information is most useful. In order to understand how the informational relevance between conditioning inputs and the score function evolves over the course of generation, we explore when guidance should be activated from an information-theoretic perspective. In this work, we formulate the diffusion trajectory as a time-dependent information bottleneck and show that the effectiveness of conditional information is not uniform throughout sampling, but becomes significantly stronger after a critical stage characterized by a Fisher-information balance condition. Motivated by this insight, we propose a training-free dynamic CFG strategy for inference. Rather than prescribing a fixed schedule in advance, our method constructs a stochastic process from conditional and unconditional score statistics and activates guidance when the estimated guidance gain crosses a prescribed threshold. This yields an adaptive activation rule that aligns condition injection with the underlying generation dynamics, while also recovering interval-based guidance as a limiting special case. Extensive experiments across diverse architectures and tasks, demonstrate that our method is effective, robust, and broadly applicable. Beyond empirical improvements, our framework provides an interpretation of dynamic guidance methods and a principled foundation for inference-time control in conditional diffusion models.

title: Measurable Semantic 3D Gaussian Splatting with Joint Region and Depth Supervision for Interactive Building Inspection
abstract: Image-based 3D reconstruction provides a scalable representation for building inspection and maintenance. However, photorealistic reconstruction alone does not fully provide the geometric measurability, semantic structure, and interactive information access required for engineering applications. This study proposes a measurable semantic 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) framework with region and depth supervision for interactive building inspection from multi-view imagery. Mask-based region supervision suppresses irrelevant backgrounds and focuses optimization on target regions. Point-wise depth supervision guides Gaussian centers toward physical surfaces using reference geometry derived from multi-view stereo (MVS) point clouds, providing geometric anchors for measuring physical dimensions and areas. A semantic Gaussian field associates learnable class features with individual Gaussian primitives, enabling semantic rendering and component-level inspection. These capabilities are operationalized through AEC-SplatTwin, an interactive building inspection platform supporting real-time visualization, semantic analysis, quantitative measurement, and multimodal large language model (MLLM)-assisted interaction. On the synthetic UAV-inspection QuakeCity and smartphone-captured HKUPB datasets, the framework reduces Gaussian-center depth MAE by 58.1% and 86.8%, while its semantic field achieves mIoU values of 0.8529 and 0.8642. On HKUPB, the mean relative errors for height, width, and area measurements are 0.33%, 1.07%, and 0.60%. These results show that the proposed framework extends 3DGS beyond visual reconstruction into a measurable, semantically structured, and interactive engineering representation for building inspection.

title: linked-rolls
abstract: A TypeScript library for digital editions of piano rolls. It reads roll copies from scans and analysis files, collates them into versions, records editorial assumptions together with the beliefs behind them, exports the edition as JSON-LD in the Roll Edition Format, and plays a version through an emulated reproducing piano.

title: Podporna orodja za raziskovanje govorjene slovenščine
abstract: Članek predstavlja pet odprtokodnih orodij za obdelavo govornih posnetkov, raz­vitih za podporo raziskovanju govorjenega slovenskega jezika. Orodja pokrivajo različne vidike dela z govornimi jezikovnimi podatki in se med seboj dopolnjujejo. Prvo orodje omogoča vsiljeno poravnavo govora z besedilom s pomočjo orodij pro­gramske knjižnice Montreal Forced Aligner. Drugo orodje je namenjeno anonimi­zaciji zvočnih posnetkov, kjer sistem samodejno prepoznane ali ročno označene dele posnetkov z osebnimi podatki nadomesti z zvočnimi maskami. Tretje orodje služi validaciji govornih posnetkov in z grafičnim vmesnikom omogoča prever­janje ujemanja posnetka s transkripcijo. Četrto orodje je akustični normalizator, ki združuje različne metode za odstranjevanje šuma in izboljšanje kakovosti pos­netkov. Peto orodje pa je grafemsko-fonemski pretvornik, ki samodejno pretvarja besedila iz običajnega grafemskega zapisa v fonetično transkripcijo.

title: Integrity Diagnostics for Cross-Silo Federated Deepfake Speech Detection Under Heterogeneity and Poisoning
abstract: Cross-silo deepfake speech detection must accommodate organizations that observe different attack profiles and channel conditions while avoiding routine centralization of raw speech. We study federated learning (FL) for a compact detector combining linear-frequency cepstral coefficients (LFCCs) with frozen WavLM representations over heterogeneous partitions derived from ASVspoof 2019 and 2021. An official-metadata audit of the historical seed-42 Client-C split reproduces the reported 2,572/3,655 (70.37%) bona-fide source overlap; a stricter unified-source audit against the complete A+B+C fit pool finds still greater dependence. We therefore repeat the principal audio evaluation with five source-disjoint splits whose holdouts are independently verified against the complete fit pool. Mean equal error rate (EER) is 3.836% for pooled centralized training, 4.622% for Federated Averaging (FedAvg), 4.095% for local C, 21.883% for local A, and 33.398% for local B. On the common Client-C holdout, A-only and B-only models transfer poorly, while FedAvg is on average 0.787 percentage points worse than pooled training and 0.527 points worse than local C; these comparisons do not establish native-domain benefit for A or B. Separately, a 20-seed controlled stress test examines integrity mechanisms under malicious participation. Increasing untargeted label-flip compromise produces progressively more negative benign--malicious update alignment and stronger aggregate-step attenuation; the signature persists across four classifier topologies and FedProx settings. Additional tests cover targeted label poisoning, a controlled trigger backdoor, zero-update free riding, and coordinated sign-flip model poisoning. We frame the contribution as an auditable experimental protocol and a bounded set of observations, not as a new detector, optimizer, attack, aggregator, or universal defense.

title: Textless Speech-to-Speech Translation from Nepali to English Using Discrete Units: A Deep Learning Approach
abstract: This study implements direct speech to speech translation eliminating the conventional need for Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) and Machine Translation (MT) by leveraging HuBERT for discrete unit extraction, a Transformer-based encoder-decoder for translation, and HiFi-GAN for speech reconstruction. Inspired by recent advances in unit-based S2ST, the model is trained on the multilingual FLEURS dataset for Nepali to English language translation. It achieved a BLEU score of 42.80, demonstrating both translation accuracy and natural-sounding speech synthesis. This work offers a scalable and effective solution for low-resource languages like Nepali.

title: A Study on the Impact of AI-Assisted Teaching Integration in College English on Students’ Writing Performance: A Case Study of Hubei Polytechnic University
abstract: At present, there are some problems in college English writing teaching, such as students ' low interest in writing, lack of personalized guidance, and low feedback efficiency. Artificial intelligence technology provides new ideas for teaching reform. In order to explore the actual impact of artificial intelligence-assisted teaching on college students’ English writing ability, this study selected two non-English major classes in Hubei Polytechnic University to carry out a one-semester quasi-experiment: 55 students in the experimental group adopted artificial intelligence-assisted teaching, and 53 students in the control group adopted traditional teaching. After the experiment, data were collected through questionnaires and in-depth interviews (10 students in each group), and the teaching effectiveness was evaluated by combining quantitative and qualitative results. The results showed that the average scores of each dimension of writing ability in the experimental class were higher than those in the control group, but did not reach a statistically significant level (P > 0.05). In the interview, the students in the experimental class had a significantly higher positive evaluation of writing interest (80%), learning effect (70%) and classroom interaction (90%). At the same time, they also put forward the problems of imperfect AI tools and easy to produce technical dependence. The control group feedback that the traditional teaching has the shortcomings of feedback lag and single form. In summary, although there is no significant statistical difference in the quantitative data, the mean value shows a positive trend of AI-assisted teaching, and the interview results also confirm that it can stimulate writing interest and improve learning experience. The teaching mode has application potential, and the teaching effect can be improved by prolonging the intervention cycle, optimizing the tools and strengthening the guidance of teachers.

title: Tracking the Invisible: Self-Supervised Wheel Track Detection with Thermal-RGB Fusion
abstract: Accurate detection of drivable area is essential for autonomous driving and advanced driver assistance systems. While state-of-the-art methods focus on general traversability estimation, they prove inadequate for snow-covered roads where following existing wheel tracks offers crucial advantages: improved traction, predictable vehicle dynamics, and verified path stability. To address this, we propose a low-cost, self-supervised approach detecting safety-critical wheel tracks using synchronized RGB-I (RGB + Long-Wave Infrared) imagery. Our method automatically generates training labels by projecting future wheel trajectories from recorded GNSS data. A neural network is designed to identify wheel tracks with the 4-channel RGB-I images from challenging, white-out road surfaces. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in visually monotonous and featureless adverse environment, offering a robust and cost-effective alternative for winter autonomy. The newly introduced ThermalTrack dataset is available at: https://digitalcommons.mtu.edu/thermaltrack/.

title: THE QUANTITY-TO-QUALITY PARADOX: How Language Models Turn Prediction into Intelligence
abstract: The large-language-model revolution demonstrates that quantitative scale alters the computational nature of a learning system:Scaled Data + Scaled Parameters + Scaled Optimization⇓Dense, Hierarchical Internal Representations⇓Invariant-Preserving Compositional Operators⇓Qualitatively Distinct Computational Regimes Prediction is an engine of algorithmic compression. A learning machine cannot predict a complex symbolic world without encoding the invariants that structure it. When that symbolic world contains physics, mathematics, algorithms, and logic, the internal representations mirror human reason.The central research question of artificial intelligence has moved beyond empirical benchmark fitting to the underlying science of representation:At what point does an internal representation cease to be a model of language and become an invariant model of reality?

title: Lost in the comments: Social context as a single‐pass jailbreak and defense on agentic platforms
abstract: Abstract As LLM‐based agents move onto multiagent platforms, they process direct prompts and surrounding social context—posts, comments, and upvotes—an attack surface that single‐turn alignment never addressed. We built a simulation of Moltbook, a social network for AI agents, and a pipeline turning 100 JailBreakBench goals into platform‐native posts with bystander comments of three valences: aggressive, ethical, and measured. Platform‐context reformatting alone raises the attack success rate (ASR) of GPT‐4o‐mini from 7% to 71%, beating a twenty‐query optimization baseline in one pass. Valence then acts as a bidirectional safety modulator: Ethical comments sharply suppress ASR, aggressive endorsements paradoxically reduce it by exposing intent, and measured, intellectually toned comments prove most dangerous, sustaining or elevating ASR. An ablation identifies valence rather than volume as key—a 35‐fold rise in upvotes leaves ASR unchanged—and every finding reproduces under an independent safety classifier with human adjudication. Ambiguous social context thus poses a greater threat than explicit pressure, while safety‐valenced signals offer a deployable defense for agentic platforms.

title: Analytical Hierarchy Process Approach in Expert Systems to Improve the Accuracy of Network Fault Detection
abstract: Computer networks play an important role in supporting information systems across sectors such as education, government, industry, and private organizations. The growing reliance on stable, reliable networks makes network disruptions a serious concern. Common issues such as internet disconnections, IP address conflicts, device failures to connect, and DNS errors often require a fast, accurate diagnosis. In practice, however, the handling of these problems is often limited by the number of available technicians and by users lack of technical understanding. This study aims to develop an expert system to automatically monitor and detect network faults. The system applies the Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP) to assign weights to each symptom through pairwise comparisons, thereby prioritizing and yielding more relevant diagnostic results. The knowledge base was developed using secondary data from previous studies that utilized forward chaining. The system is implemented as a web-based application with a user-friendly interface. System evaluation was conducted using 50 network fault test cases, and the results showed that the proposed system achieved 92% accuracy, 91% precision, 90% recall, and an F1-score of 90.5% based on expert validation. In addition, the AHP consistency test produced a Consistency Ratio (CR) value of 0.08, indicating that the pairwise comparison matrix was logically consistent. These results demonstrate that the proposed system improves the efficiency and effectiveness of network fault diagnosis for both technical and non-technical users.

title: Design and performance analysis of a six-state QKD over FSO and optical fiber utilizing switch-controlled polarization generation for secure optical communications
abstract: Abstract Quantum key distribution (QKD) is a process that utilizes the principles of quantum mechanics to securely share a secret key between two parties, ensuring unconditional security. Diverse QKD protocols are established to guarantee the security and integrity of information against any attempts by an eavesdropper monitoring the transferred photons. One of these protocols is the six-state protocol. This work employs OptiSystem 21.1 simulation software to design and emulate the six-state protocol, wherein polarization states are produced through random switching control rather than optical modulators. The protocol’s performance, indicated by quantum bit error rate and secure key rate, is analytically examined for both free space optical (FSO) channel and optical fiber channel, incorporating parameters from two types of commercial single-photon detectors to enhance realism. The maximum secure key rate attains 5.439 Mbps at 10 km of optical fiber, in contrast to 1.674 Mbps at 0.2 km under clear weather conditions in the FSO quantum channel utilizing ID 281 single-photon detector modules across both channels. The maximum distance that guarantees secure key rate with ID 281 for FSO channel is 2 km with 1760 bps with heavy haze compared to 100 km optical fiber with secure key rate of 15,000 bps.

title: Factoring some integers using Shor’s algorithm on real quantum hardware
abstract: Abstract Experimental realizations of Shor’s algorithm on NISQ devices often rely on heavy circuit compilation, inadvertently encodingprior knowledge of the solution and bypassing the core challenge of quantum arithmetic. In this work, we present a transparent,hardware execution baseline for the quantum order-finding routine that maintains explicit modular exponentiation, but focusingon structured composite integers that simplify modular arithmetic. We mitigate the circuit depth by targeting moduli composedof Fermat primes, where the multiplication constants ck = A2kmod N simplify to either identities or powers of two, requiringonly simple bit-shift operations. We executed this explicit arithmetic approach on IBM superconducting hardware for N ∈{51, 85, 255, 771}. For moduli up to N = 255, we observed Hellinger fidelities up to 0.946. For N = 771, we quantitativelydemonstrate the signal degradation caused by increased circuit depth and accumulated hardware noise. By reporting raw anddevice-compiled gate counts alongside intermediate arithmetic validation, this methodology provides an experimental proxyfor studying circuit depth and noise in structured instances of order-finding, establishing a reproducible reference point forevaluating future hardware-aware optimizations.

title: Many Scores Force Many Reads: An Optimality Proof for Score of Parentheses
abstract: LeetCode Problem 856, Score of Parentheses, admits a one-pass algorithm using $O(n)$ time and $O(1)$ auxiliary registers. Its correctness follows from a local interpretation: every occurrence of () contributes a power of two determined by its nesting depth. The space bound is immediately optimal in the usual programming-challenge model, but the linear-time bound is less obvious. In particular, a direct adversary that forces an algorithm to inspect every character is difficult to maintain under the promise that the input is balanced. We instead prove a counting lower bound. For every $k$, we construct $2^k$ balanced parenthesis strings of the same length $4k+2$, all having distinct scores. The construction encodes each bit using one of two operations, changing a current score $v$ to either $2v+1$ or $2v+2$. Consequently, any deterministic character-query decision tree computing the score must have depth at least $k$. A two-character padding argument extends the result to every even input length, proving an $Ω(n)$ worst-case time lower bound. The one-pass algorithm is therefore asymptotically optimal in the unit-cost RAM model.

title: JitterVLA: A Replay Benchmark for Motion Quality in VLA-Driven Human-Robot Manipulation
abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies issue sparse targets whose arrival at the robot controller is delayed and irregular, so a reasonable predicted action can still produce abrupt motion near people. Remedies are evaluated on different streams, delays and metrics. JitterVLA replays identical commands and arrival traces through alternative controllers, isolating the controller's effect. We apply it to synthetic reaches, hand trajectories from 20 people, three open VLA pipelines (838 episodes) and a physical UR3. Interpolation lowered modeled p99 jerk for every source, by 83% (615 to 106 m/s^3) on human motion with 200 ms delay, at a 2.0 cm tracking cost, and the effect replicated on 598 new episodes; jerk-limited generation lowered jerk further at a larger cost. Entropy-discontinuity associations had opposite, replicated signs in two pipelines, and entropy gating helped in one but not the other. On the UR3, interpolation lowered accelerometer-derived jerk by 3.0-14.0% in all six exploratory pairs, while a position-derived metric did not resolve the contrast. JitterVLA supports screening before human-centred studies; code and data will be released.

title: ECGWmark: Deep Watermarking for Electrocardiogram Signals
abstract: Secure transmission of electrocardiogram (ECG) signals remains a major challenge in telecardiology. While traditional mathematical watermarking can embed patient metadata directly into ECG signals, it is highly fragile against temporal desynchronization such as circular phase shifts. In contrast, existing deep watermarking approaches for temporal signals, such as audio, typically rely on lossy quantization, which compromises the high-frequency micro-morphological details critical for clinical diagnosis. To bridge this gap, we propose ECGWmark, a fully convolutional and quantization-free deep watermarking framework for medical time-series. ECGWmark operates in a continuous, full-resolution latent space and utilizes a localized frame-level mechanism to improve the robustness to severe desynchronization. Crucially, we introduce a differentiable Physiological Loss guided by a clinical classifier to preserve diagnostic semantics. Experiments on the benchmark MIT-BIH database show that ECGWmark maintains channel-bit extraction accuracy above 90% under the evaluated circular temporal shifts. Furthermore, under a rigorous inter-patient diagnostic evaluation, Class-V sensitivity changes from 71.97% to 76.50%, whereas Macro-F1 changes from 35.25% to 34.71% and Class-S sensitivity from 8.89% to 1.39%; these results indicate mixed class-level effects.

title: VDFedDiff: a novel versatile defense scheme against adversarial attacks in federated diffusion models
abstract: Abstract Federated learning (FL) enables multiple clients to collaboratively train machine learning models without sharing their raw data, making it a promising paradigm for privacy-sensitive generative applications. However, diffusion models trained in federated environments remain vulnerable to backdoor, evasion, and model-poisoning attacks, which can degrade generative quality or induce attacker-specified behaviors. Existing Byzantine-robust aggregation methods primarily mitigate anomalous client updates but do not address coordinate-localized poisoning or adversarial perturbations in the diffusion latent space. Meanwhile, existing defenses for diffusion models are generally designed for centralized settings and therefore cannot directly handle malicious client updates in federated training. To address these limitations, we propose VDFedDiff, a multi-level defense framework for federated diffusion models. VDFedDiff integrates three complementary components: Adaptive Trust Scoring (ATS), which dynamically reduces the influence of anomalous client updates; Adversarial Gradient Filtering (AGF), which suppresses coordinate-wise malicious deviations through median- and median-absolute-deviation-based filtering; and Latent-Space Purification (LSP), which introduces time-aware stochastic regularization to weaken adversarial alignment during local diffusion training. Experiments on CIFAR-10, CelebA, and LSUN-Bedroom under backdoor, evasion, and model-poisoning attacks demonstrate that VDFedDiff consistently improves attack resilience while preserving generative quality. On non-IID CIFAR-10 under combined backdoor and model-poisoning attacks, VDFedDiff reduces the FID from 46.8 to 28.3 and the attack success rate from 72.5% to 23.8% compared with undefended FedAvg. It also introduces only 6.1% additional per-round computation time and no additional communication overhead in the evaluated setting. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of combining client-level, coordinate-level, and latent-level protection for securing federated diffusion training.

title: LLMDPA: pre-execution privacy auditing of DP-SGD via evidence-constrained semantic analysis
abstract: Abstract Privacy auditing has emerged as a critical component for safeguarding data privacy in machine learning models. Existing empirical auditing methods heavily rely on model runtime states or post-deployment interfaces, resulting in substantial time costs and limited source-level localization of leakage causes. In contrast, the theoretical guarantees of provable privacy mechanisms provide a basis for efficient privacy auditing with source-level traceability before model training. However, the validity of such auditing depends on the semantic consistency of the underlying implementation, which remains difficult for current automated methods to verify due to limited privacy-specific reasoning and explicit evidence modeling. To address this gap, we formalize the Pre-execution Privacy Auditing paradigm and instantiate it for DP-SGD through LLMDPA, an automated framework based on evidence-constrained semantic analysis. LLMDPA constructs a structured Evidence Chain to constrain LLM-based adjudication and identify hidden semantic failures in DP-SGD implementations. Evaluations on real-world and controlled benchmarks show that LLMDPA achieves global precision ranging from 98.82 to 100% and global F1-scores ranging from 0.9091 to 0.9677 across four LLM configurations, outperforming conventional static and vanilla LLM baselines. Moreover, LLMDPA audits a repository in approximately 50 s, providing a scalable and efficient complement to scale-sensitive attack evaluations. Overall, LLMDPA provides an interpretable and evidence-traceable instantiation of Pre-execution Privacy Auditing for DP-SGD.

title: Towards Dynamical Casimir sourced N00N states for quantum sensing
abstract: We explore the uncorrelated photon saturation of N00N state based phase measurements. In the case of a single mode, any combination of coherent and squeezed vacuum states exhibits stringent upper limits to the entangled photon flux [1], beyond which sub shot noise precision is inaccessible. These upper limits prevent single mode N00N state phase measurement approaches from reaching the performance of their classical counterparts. Turning to multimode squeezed states, in particular sourced by the dynamical Casimir effect (DCE) in a THz modulation approach proposed in [2], we characterize the resulting improved ranges of permissible photon fluxes.

evidence.title: Towards Dynamical Casimir sourced N00N states for quantum sensing
evidence.abstract: We explore the uncorrelated photon saturation of N00N state based phase measurements. In the case of a single mode, any combination of coherent and squeezed vacuum states exhibits stringent upper limits to the entangled photon flux [1], beyond which sub shot noise precision is inaccessible. These upper limits prevent single mode N00N state phase measurement approaches from reaching the performance of their classical counterparts. Turning to multimode squeezed states, in particular sourced by the dynamical Casimir effect (DCE) in a THz modulation approach proposed in [2], we characterize the resulting improved ranges of permissible photon fluxes.

title: Implicit Category Projection‐Enhanced Multimodal Seq2Seq for Ensuring Accurate Day‐Ahead PV Forecasting Under Transitional Weather
abstract: This chapter focuses on improving day-ahead photovoltaic (PV) power forecasting under transitional weather conditions, where rapid shifts in meteorological patterns often lead to significant prediction errors. To address this challenge, a multimodal Seq2Seq forecasting framework enhanced with an implicit category projection (ICP) mechanism is proposed, aiming to better capture the complex and dynamic relationships between PV generation and weather variations. The chapter first introduces an ICP mechanism that groups PV generation profiles through density-weighted clustering and supervised category pretraining. This design enables the model to uncover latent generation patterns and more effectively distinguish between different operating conditions, thereby improving its ability to model non-stationary behaviors under transitional weather. Building on this, a time-aligned multimodal encoder is developed to handle heterogeneous input data. It performs temporal category projection via gated feature embeddings, allowing adaptive emphasis on relevant features, and incorporates meteorological information through a step-wise feature fusion module. This structure ensures effective alignment and interaction between PV and weather sequences. Experimental results on representative open PV datasets demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves improved accuracy and robustness, particularly in scenarios with rapidly changing weather. Overall, the approach provides a practical and scalable solution for enhancing the reliability of day-ahead PV forecasting in real-world grid operations.

title: DPAL: A Test-Time Adaptation Loss for Financial Time Series Forecasting
abstract: Test-time adaptation (TTA) enables time series forecasters to update after deployment as new observations become available. However, adaptation objectives that focus primarily on prediction errors at individual time steps do not fully address the needs of financial time series forecasting. In addition to pointwise return fitting, return direction and the price trajectories reconstructed from sequences of returns are also important. To better account for these properties, we introduce Direction- and Price-Aware Adaptation Loss (DPAL), which combines pointwise return fitting with directional and price-calibration terms. We apply DPAL within existing TSF-TTA frameworks without modifying the source forecaster or the adapter architecture. Across a diverse collection of financial datasets, DPAL reduces reconstructed-price mean squared error in most evaluated settings.

title: Memory-Coupled Unlearning for Data-Absent Identity Forgetting
abstract: Machine unlearning aims to reduce the influence of designated training data from a trained model while preserving its utility on retained data. Identity-level unlearning is particularly challenging when only limited target-specific information is available when a forgetting request is processed. In this work, we propose Memory-Coupled Unlearning (MCU), a framework that augments a host model with a Modern Hopfield Network (MHN) serving as a controllable external identity-prototype memory. During prototype construction, feature representations associated with each training identity are aggregated into identity prototypes and stored in the MHN. A Prototype Adaptation Network (PAN) transforms the retrieved memory representation, while a Dependency Gating Unit (DGU) controls its contribution to downstream prediction. When an identity is requested to be forgotten, MCU first removes the corresponding prototype from the external memory and subsequently readapts the model using limited support information associated with the target identities together with retained data. Importantly, in this work, ``data-absent'' specifically refers to the absence of the complete original forget set during request-time gradient-based readaptation; retained data may still be used to preserve downstream-task utility. Experiments based on the identity-partitioning and one-shot support construction of 1-SHUI show that MCU achieves a favorable empirical trade-off among model utility, membership distinguishability, and request-time computational efficiency compared with the evaluated baselines. These results provide empirical evidence for the potential of controllable external memory in machine unlearning, rather than a formal guarantee of complete information removal.
